notes.md:
#### What's new

- **Runtime directory names starting `carlos-` are reserved.** `carlos ship` now refuses an app whose capabilities set a `runtime_dir` beginning with `carlos-`, the same way it already refused `systemd-` names. The platform uses that prefix for its own directories. Pick another name if your app used one.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Boxes first, then the console. The box roll sets up the console's runtime directory. The console's next deploy, or any restart, creates `/run/carlos-console` and the console's socket in it. Nothing restarts the console for you.
- **Tunnel hubs reach the console through a socket.** A hub passes fleet boxes' calls to the console through `/run/carlos-console/fleet.sock`, and checks the listener is the console's user before it sends anything. `CARLOS_REPLICA_CONSOLE_ADDR` in `host.env` still wins when it is set. `carlos system status` shows, under each box with a console, the last call's result, how it reached the console and when, and why the socket isn't ready if it isn't.
- **The `host.env` line can go.** If you set `CARLOS_REPLICA_CONSOLE_ADDR` on a hub by hand, remove it once `carlos system status` no longer shows "socket not ready" for that box, then restart `carlos-edge`. Check that the next call shows `socket` and `ok`.
- **The console must not run as root.** The socket is used only when the console runs as a non-root user, because a root listener can't be proved to be the console. A hub whose console runs as root falls back to `CARLOS_REPLICA_CONSOLE_ADDR` or the old route scan.
- **The old route scan is narrower, and goes next release.** Without the env line or the socket, the hub still looks for a console route, but now accepts only a loopback TCP route. The next release removes the scan.
- **An app that already has a `carlos-` runtime directory** keeps it, but can't be shipped again with it. If it claims `carlos-console`, the hub on that box won't use the socket.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **Move a domain here from another registrar.** Choose Move to Carloku on the domain's page, enter its transfer code and check out. Your card is held, not charged, until the current registrar accepts the move. If the move does not go through, the hold is released or your payment is refunded in full. The domain keeps the nameservers it uses today, so its DNS and email don't change. From the CLI, run `carlos domains transfer <name> --auth-code -`. Moves are only offered for the domain endings your deployment has turned on.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Boxes first, then the console.
- **Coming from v0.43.1 or older?** Read the v0.43.2 notes too. Coming from v0.42.1, also read the v0.43.0 and v0.43.1 notes: v0.43.0 adds settings and rollback limits that apply to you.
- **Transfers stay off until you turn them on.** Nothing changes until your domain catalog sets `"transferable": true` on a TLD. Mark only TLDs where a transfer adds one year to the existing expiry, as `com` and `net` do. The optional `transfer` map sets the one-year transfer price per currency; a currency missing from it uses the `renew` price. The TLD's `max_cost` also caps the registrar's transfer cost. The domain buying guide has the details.
- **Unknown transfers need a listed store operator.** If the registrar's outcome is unknown, the console alerts the operator and leaves the transfer open until the registrar answers or an operator resolves it. Only a person listed as a store operator can call `POST /api/cli/system/domains/purchases/{id}/resolve`; service credentials and ordinary account-owner access cannot. Set `outcome` to `failed` or `completed` for an unknown live transfer. `completed` requires the registrar to show the domain in this account. If a captured failed transfer's refund has been refused at least three times, refund it another way, then use `refunded_outside`.
- **New alert: registrations nearing expiry.** The console alerts the operator once when any registration, bought or transferred, is within 60 days of expiry, including registrations that have already expired. Domains are not renewed automatically, so renew them at the registrar.
- **Rollback limit.** Once any transfer exists, do not roll a console back below v0.43.3: an older console would handle transfers as purchases. Before the first transfer, rolling back to v0.43.2 is fine.

#### What's new

- **Pre-issued attached custom domains work through every edge as soon as DNS switches.** When a deployment has issued an attached custom domain's certificate before its DNS moves here, the box that hosts it serves the domain, and other boxes pass requests to that box instead of answering `503` "Almost ready" for 5 to 7 minutes.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Boxes first, then the console.
- **Coming from v0.42.1?** Read the v0.43.0 and v0.43.1 notes too: v0.43.0 adds settings and rollback limits that apply to you.
- **Pre-issued custom domains are published before they point here.** With `CARLOS_DNS01_ZONES` and `CARLOS_DNS01_ACCOUNTS` set, a box publishes an attached hostname in a listed zone when the hostname belongs to a listed account and a current matching certificate is on the box, before its DNS points here. Other boxes pass its requests to the box that hosts it, so they no longer answer `503` "Almost ready" for 5 to 7 minutes after the switch. Without both settings, nothing changes.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **Custom domains follow a move to a new DNS host.** When a custom domain moves to a new DNS host, the platform's fresh DNS lookup now asks the domain's parent zone which name servers hold it, instead of using the box's cached list, which can stay out of date until its TTL runs out. Before, a box could keep asking the old DNS host, and the domain could stay unpublished on every box but its home box, so other regions answered "unknown host". If the parent zone gives no usable answer, the lookup uses the cached list, as before.

This release also carries everything in v0.43.0. If you skipped v0.43.0, read its notes too.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Boxes first, then the console.
- **SES topic message.** The console no longer logs a parse error at start for the message Amazon SES sends when it validates the console's event topic. The console now accepts that message, counts nothing for it, and logs one line saying the topic reaches it.
- **Coming from v0.42.1?** This release replaces v0.43.0, and v0.43.0's operator notes apply:
  - **What can't be rolled back below v0.43.0 once it's used.** The console refuses a fleet size until the console and every box the app can run on use v0.43.0 or later. It refuses an egress range while any currently reporting box in the deployment uses an older release. Once either feature is in an app's policy, an older box treats the whole policy as unverifiable and closes its egress allows and sizes. The console refuses to publish a release below v0.43.0 to a channel followed by an app using a fleet size. If the console is rolled back below v0.43.0, a policy using either feature expires after 72 hours and the boxes close its allows and sizes.
  - **Before a box takes a fleet size.** Set `CARLOS_FLEET` in the box's root-owned `host.env`. Its effective sandbox must be systemd, not gVisor, so set `CARLOS_EXEC_SANDBOX=systemd` if needed. The box refuses a fleet size without a fleet name, with gVisor active, or when the size leaves too little memory.
  - **16g and 24g on 32 GiB boxes.** An overlap deploy reserves the new copy's full memory limit before it starts, and the old and new limits together must fit the box's fleet budget: its memory less an eighth, about 27 GiB on a 32 GiB box. The console accepts 16g and 24g as sizes, but replacing a 16g or 24g build with another build at the same size is refused before the new build starts. The old build keeps serving, and the instance gets one warning event. Use 12g or below for same-size overlap deploys on 32 GiB boxes.
  - **Certificates before DNS moves.** Set `CARLOS_DNS01_ZONES` and `CARLOS_DNS01_ACCOUNTS`, and configure a DNS provider. For DNSimple, leave `CARLOS_DNS_PROVIDER` unset or set it to `dnsimple`, then set `CARLOS_DNSIMPLE_TOKEN`. For Route 53, set `CARLOS_DNS_PROVIDER=route53` and give the box AWS credentials with DNS access. The issuing box then obtains certificates for attached custom hostnames in those zones and accounts over DNS-01 before DNS points here. Every box can serve the certificate when DNS switches. If either list is unset, this feature is off.
  - **Store versioning is off by default.** To turn it on, use AWS S3: set `CARLOS_STORE_BACKEND=aws`, leave `CARLOS_STORE_ENDPOINT` unset, and set `CARLOS_STORE_REGION`, `CARLOS_STORE_BUCKET_PREFIX`, and `CARLOS_STORE_USER_BOUNDARY`. Set `CARLOS_STORE_VERSIONING=1` on the console and `store_versioning = true` in the region host module on the console's box. Use the same dedicated prefix for `CARLOS_STORE_BUCKET_PREFIX` and `store_bucket_prefix`; it must end in `-store-` and must not overlap deployment, data, staging, or fleet bucket prefixes. Earlier versions expire after `keep_days`, from 30 to 365 days, and that setting can only increase. Versioning cannot be used with media conversion or browser uploads.
  - **The console database gains three columns and an index** for demo claim codes.
  - **HA departures page once.** A departed group member that this box never saw now pages once instead of every hour. An older box keeps the hourly retry.
  - **Group rolls.** `carlos system group` reads a member's status once more when the read that proves a revoke is cut off, instead of stopping with the transaction open.

#### What's new

- **Bigger sizes on your own fleet.** Apps whose instances run on your account's own fleet can now use 4g, 6g, 8g, 12g, 16g, 24g, 32g, 48g, 96g and 192g. The small to xlarge sizes, and apps on shared boxes, are unchanged.
- **Egress to private ranges.** `carlos apps set --egress-allow` now takes private ranges, such as `10.0.64.0/20` or `fd00:5::/64`, as well as single addresses, so a managed database that moves within its subnets on failover stays reachable. A range can be no wider than /16 for IPv4 or /48 for IPv6, and you can still list at most 8 entries.
- **Store versioning, when your deployment enables it.** `carlos store versioning on`, `carlos store versions` and `carlos store restore` keep earlier object versions and copy one back. `--keep-days` sets retention from 30 to 365 days, and retention can only increase. Once versioning is on, the platform has no off command. Earlier versions count toward storage limits. Versioned stores cannot use media conversion or browser uploads.
- **Rootfs apps know their memory.** The web process and every worker of a rootfs app now get `CARLOS_MEMORY_MIB`, the memory limit they start with, so an app server can set its process counts from its size.
- **Demo claim links carry their own code.** The claim link you hand over no longer contains the token that updates the demo. Demos made before this release still claim as before until they expire.
- **More security headers for static sites.** A static site's `_headers` may now set `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and `X-DNS-Prefetch-Control`.
- **Fleet apps see the real visitor.** An app reached through a hub on your own fleet now sees the visitor's address the hub saw, not the hub's, so per-visitor limits work.
- **Analytics for busy apps.** The analytics tab no longer fails for an app with more than 25 referrers in the period.

Update your CLI to use these.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Boxes first, then the console.
- **What can't be rolled back below v0.43.0 once it's used.** The console refuses a fleet size until the console and every box the app can run on use v0.43.0 or later. It refuses an egress range while any currently reporting box in the deployment uses an older release. Once either feature is in an app's policy, an older box treats the whole policy as unverifiable and closes its egress allows and sizes. The console refuses to publish a release below v0.43.0 to a channel followed by an app using a fleet size. If the console is rolled back below v0.43.0, a policy using either feature expires after 72 hours and the boxes close its allows and sizes.
- **Before a box takes a fleet size.** Set `CARLOS_FLEET` in the box's root-owned `host.env`. Its effective sandbox must be systemd, not gVisor, so set `CARLOS_EXEC_SANDBOX=systemd` if needed. The box refuses a fleet size without a fleet name, with gVisor active, or when the size leaves too little memory.
- **Certificates before DNS moves.** Set `CARLOS_DNS01_ZONES` and `CARLOS_DNS01_ACCOUNTS`, and configure a DNS provider. For DNSimple, leave `CARLOS_DNS_PROVIDER` unset or set it to `dnsimple`, then set `CARLOS_DNSIMPLE_TOKEN`. For Route 53, set `CARLOS_DNS_PROVIDER=route53` and give the box AWS credentials with DNS access. The issuing box then obtains certificates for attached custom hostnames in those zones and accounts over DNS-01 before DNS points here. Every box can serve the certificate when DNS switches. If either list is unset, this feature is off.
- **Store versioning is off by default.** It requires AWS S3 with `CARLOS_STORE_BACKEND=aws`, no `CARLOS_STORE_ENDPOINT`, `CARLOS_STORE_VERSIONING=1` on the console, and `store_versioning = true` in the region host module on the console's box. Use a dedicated `store_bucket_prefix` ending in `-store-`, with no overlap with deployment, data, staging or fleet bucket prefixes. Earlier versions expire after the store's `keep_days`, from 30 to 365 days, and that setting can only increase. Versioning cannot be used with media conversion or browser uploads.
- **The console database gains three columns and an index** for demo claim codes.
- **HA departures page once.** A departed group member that this box never saw now pages once instead of every hour. An older box keeps the hourly retry.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **A path prefix reaches its app on any box.** When a hostname splits its traffic by path (for example, `example.com/shop` served by another app), the prefix now reaches its target app whichever box of the deployment serves that app, and whichever box the request arrives on. The box that receives the request makes at most one hop to the target's box, with the Host and the path unchanged. If the target is a region HA app, the hop goes to the box that serves it now. Before, a prefix whose target lived on another box fell through to the hostname's own app.
- **Pages reached across boxes are not response-cached.** A page served through a prefix whose app is on another box is never read from or written to the response cache, so every cacheable page request reaches the app and a hibernating app wakes for it. Prefixes whose app is on the same box use the response cache as before.
- **Imports.** While a hostname's own app is being imported, the import gate returns `503` with `Retry-After` until commit for that hostname's own route and prefixes to apps on the same box, except the app's verify requests. A prefix whose app is on another box keeps serving while the hostname's own app imports.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Boxes first, then the console.
- **Nothing changes until a path map names an app on another box.** Before you roll, run `go run ./scripts/pathmapcheck -bucket <control bucket> -region <region>` from a checkout of the platform repository at this release, once for each control bucket. It only reads published path claims and each box's edges file. It is a repository tool, not part of the release. If it prints `FAIL`, at least one target is missing from a box that serves its front, a front or target has no serving box, or a claim or edges file could not be listed, read, or decoded. Resolve the report before rolling. Roll every box before anything publishes such a map, because a box still on an older release can answer a hop to a region HA app with a 503. The repository's `docs/superpowers/runbooks/path-routes-across-boxes-rollout.md` has the steps.
- **Coming from v0.40.x or v0.41.0?** Read the v0.41.0 and v0.42.0 notes too. Before you run `carlos system seeds-floor publish --min-release v0.41.0`, roll every box to v0.41.0 or later and make sure each box keeps a `carlos.prev` at v0.41.0 or later.
- **Media conversion stays off by default.** Nothing changes until you apply the media engine module, set `store_conversion = true` in the region host module, set `CARLOS_STORE_CONVERSION=1`, and set `CARLOS_MEDIA_ENGINE` to the media engine module's output. If conversion is on, roll the console and the engine image from the same release.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **Media conversion limits from measured runs.** Conversion is still off until your operator sets up the conversion engine. Where it is on, the short class now refuses a video above 1080p with `needs_long_class`, however short the video is: send the same request again with `"class": "long"`. In the long class, HDR video up to 1080p converts up to 75 minutes. Other video keeps its maximum: 2 hours up to 1080p, 30 minutes above it. A minute of video above 1080p now counts as 2 media minutes against your account's allowance. Video up to 1080p still counts 1 and audio 0.1. Video is encoded with x264's `medium` preset instead of `veryfast`.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Boxes first, then the console.
- **Coming from v0.40.x?** Read the v0.41.0 notes too. Before you run `carlos system seeds-floor publish --min-release v0.41.0`, roll every box to v0.41.0 or later and make sure each box keeps a `carlos.prev` at v0.41.0 or later.
- **Always-on instances come back sooner after an agent restart.** On a fleet box, an always-on instance with a single copy was down about 33 s while its box's agent restarted. A replica that is still fenced is now tried again on the next 2-second tick, instead of being treated as a failed build with the old 1 to 16 s backoff. An agent that has just restarted reads the instance record directly instead of refusing the wake until its first scan.
- **Media conversion stays off by default.** Nothing changes until you apply the media engine module, set `store_conversion = true` in the region host module, set `CARLOS_STORE_CONVERSION=1`, and set `CARLOS_MEDIA_ENGINE` to the media engine module's output. If conversion is on, roll the console and the engine image from the same release. An older image refuses this console's video jobs, and an older console refuses this image's HDR results. The first push of the engine image to ECR now succeeds, and a plan right after applying the media engine module no longer replaces its task definitions.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **Start an instance from a database file.** `carlos instances create --app <app> --host <host> --seed-file <file>` starts a new instance from a SQLite database file you already have, up to 4 GiB. The CLI uploads it, the console checks that it is a sound database, and the new instance starts from it the first time it wakes. This works for an app that runs in a region and for an app on a fleet of your own. You can't combine it with `--from`, and the new instance is an ordinary one, so `--kind`, `--addr` and `--role` don't apply. If the upload or the check fails, nothing is created, and the hostname is free again once its box has cleaned up. On a fleet of your own, the fleet must have exactly one active box, and that box must keep each instance in its own directory. If a copy of the data is left in the fleet's bucket, the hostname stays taken until you remove that copy, and the delete answer names where it is. Your operator has to publish the seeds floor for this release before `--seed-file` works.
- **Live pages keep up with more viewers.** The edge now holds up to 1,000 event streams opened with `carlos_hold=1` per host, up from 64. Before, viewers past the 64th on one app got a page that never updated.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Boxes first, then the console.
- **Seed files need the seeds floor raised, and the raise is deployment-wide.** Roll every box, in every region and on every customer fleet, so that both the running binary and its rollback binary `carlos.prev` are on this release, before you run `carlos system seeds-floor publish`. A publish from this release's console raises the floor to protocol 4 for the whole deployment. From then on, `carlos instances create --from`, `carlos instances import` and demo claims are refused wherever a box is below that, until it is rolled. Until the floor is raised, `--seed-file` is refused. For a seed file on a customer fleet, the fleet's box must run this release and keep each instance in its own directory (the nested layout).
- **Held event streams have new caps.** One host can hold up to 1,000 streams on a box. The box's total now comes from its memory instead of a fixed 4,096: about 1,000 on a 1 or 2 GiB box, 2,000 at 4 GiB, 4,000 at 8 GiB and 8,000 at 16 GiB, and never more than its open-file limit allows. Streams that arrive through a fleet or linked deployment's channel are capped at 64 in all, so one busy page can't stall the other apps on that box.
- **Platform accounts: quieter held creates.** When the console holds a customer create because the bucket and the console disagree, it now retries at most once every 5 minutes, and logs the held line at most that often. After a repair, the create can take up to 5 minutes to go through. Expired per-customer credentials bound to an app are now deleted with other expired credentials, except on a console with `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM` on, where they stay until their app is purged. They already stopped working when they expired.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **Domains for the whole account.** Each account has a Domains page in the console. It lists every domain the account uses, whether bought here, still being bought, or registered elsewhere, with each address under its domain, and each domain has a page of its own. You can buy a domain there in three steps, for an app or for no app yet. From a terminal, `carlos domains list --all` shows the same list and any account member can run it; `carlos domains buy <domain> --not-yet` buys a domain without pointing it anywhere, and `carlos domains point <domain> --app <app>` sets up the domain and its `www` for an app later. A domain is registered to a contact you save once and reuse: `carlos domains contacts` lists them, and `contacts add`, `contacts edit` and `contacts remove` change them. Editing a contact changes future purchases only. Only account owners can buy domains, point them or use saved contacts. An account that holds a domain, or has a purchase in progress, can't be deleted.
- **Deploy a static site from CI.** A service token with the Publish role can now give a static app its first host at `<app>.<account>.<apps-domain>`, so `carlos deploy --kind static` uses that host from CI with `CARLOS_SERVICE_TOKEN` and `CARLOS_CONSOLE`.
- **Platform accounts.** An operator can let an account run customer accounts of its own. That account's platform credential creates and manages them with `carlos platform customers` and mints a short-lived credential for one customer with `carlos platform credentials mint`. Nothing changes until an operator grants an account with `carlos accounts platform`.
- **Video and audio conversion, plus browser uploads.** `carlos media convert` starts a conversion and can follow its job, while `carlos media status` shows the job. `carlos store uploads` lets browsers upload large files straight to an app's store. Conversion is off until your operator sets up the conversion engine. Browser uploads are off until you enable them for an app.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production.
- **Every wake protects the database before the app starts.** Writes an app made while starting, such as migrations, could be missed by its replica, and a later restore could fail as a malformed database. Now each wake first checks that the database is exactly as its last clean close left it, and holds it so the app's first writes reach the replica. If that can't be proven, the wake uploads a full copy of the database before it serves. Every database takes a full copy on its first wake after the upgrade, so expect one larger upload per database. A wake whose replica can't be reached now fails instead of serving without replication, and `carlos logs --stream platform` shows `replicate <host>: ...`. The clean-close records are kept in the agent's data directory, under `.continuity`.
- **Media conversion is off by default.** Nothing changes until you apply the media engine module, set `store_conversion` on the region host module, and set `CARLOS_STORE_CONVERSION=1` and `CARLOS_MEDIA_ENGINE` on a console. `carlos system media status` shows whether the engine is ready.
- **Platform accounts are off until you grant one.** `carlos accounts platform --account <sqid> --grant` turns it on for one account, and `--revoke` stops its credentials at once. Customer accounts it creates skip billing and the free-account cap, and their plan notices go to the platform's owners.
- **Domain buying stays off while `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM` is on.** On such a console the buy pages and the CLI's buy are refused. When a bought domain's records are removed, alias records are now deleted before the records they point at.

notes.md:
#### What's new

The CLI has no new commands.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production.
- **Instance control gets more memory.** `carlos-instance-control` now has a `MemoryMax=256M` limit, up from 64M. Starting an instance launches short-lived helper processes of about 10 to 17 MB each inside that limit, so several starts at once could exceed 64M. When that happened, the kernel killed instance control and the starts failed. This occurred while one member of a region was taking over several hosts. 256M covers roughly twelve concurrent starts at those sizes. It is a limit, not memory set aside.
- **A box updated by an older build catches up at its next hourly adopt pass.** On a box with claims enabled, an updater older than this release can leave out the claim mode's 192 MiB runtime memory target. On a box with the demo build worker enabled, it can leave out the worker's 1 GiB memory limit and 768 MiB runtime target. The next adopt pass rewrites the unit and restarts instance control, with no manual restart. On a region HA group member, that pass rewrites the unit only under a repair permit.

#### What's new

- **Named units install when a directory on the console guard path is not trusted by root.** In v0.40.0, a box rejected every declaration delivered by `carlos system named-units put`, and local `carlos system named-units install` rejected it too, with "console guard marker: permission denied" if any directory in the path to `/opt/carlos/system/guard` was not owned by root, was writable by group or others, or lacked read and execute permission for group and others. Such a box cannot hold a guard that root trusts, so it is now treated as unguarded and the declaration installs. `carlos system named-units show` reports "console guard not readable here, so treated as unguarded", and the box's journal includes the same text. A marker file that is untrusted while its directory path is trusted is still refused.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production.
- **When a box picks up a declaration.** The box installs a parameter value on its next config pass, within the hour. A config write starts an earlier pass only when the app you write to runs as a named unit on that box.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **Declare a box's named units from your own machine.** `carlos system named-units put --instance <instance-id> --aws-region <region> <file>` validates the named-unit declaration and writes it to that box's SSM parameter, `/carlos/host/named-units/<instance-id>`. You need `ssm:PutParameter` on that path, not root access to the box. A declaration that fails the file checks is refused before anything is written. The box applies its additional local safety check when it reads the parameter. Use the box's own AWS region for `--aws-region`. The box installs it on its next config pass (any config write to an app on that box starts one) or within the hour. `carlos system named-units show` prints the stored value beside what the box last reported. To clear a box's units, put `{"schema":1,"units":[]}`. Deleting the parameter does not clear them: the box keeps the file it has.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production.
- **Named units: what a box needs.** Group-launched boxes and managed fleet boxes skip the parameter. A box with an invalid fleet setting reads it instead and reports the result. For a fixed box, the box's role needs `ssm:GetParameter` on `/carlos/host/named-units/<instance-id>` in the box's own region. A role that may read `/carlos/*` already has that permission. `carlos system named-units install` on the box is unchanged.
- **A database file could stay open after a snapshot was cancelled.** On instances without region HA, a snapshot cancelled at the wrong moment held the database's write-ahead log open until the edge restarted. Every snapshot now closes its upload, whatever happens to it.
- **Storage generations for region HA groups, off until you turn them on.** This release carries per-holder storage generations for region HA hosts. Nothing changes until a group sets `CARLOS_HA_GENERATIONS` to `on` or `fast`. Once a host has generations, `carlos db pull` and `carlos db query` from an older CLI are refused with a message to run `carlos update`. Run `carlos ops ha-generations list|verify|point` on the affected box as the `carlos` user to recover a region HA host whose wake was refused for a storage-generation problem. `point` can permanently discard newer transactions and requires `--yes`.

- **Roll order.** Roll your development deployment first, then production. Before disabling client IP preservation, make sure every target's edge reports `idle`.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **Declare mail when you deploy.** `carlos deploy` and `carlos canary` now take `--mail submit`, the same as `carlos ship`. If email submission is on for the app, a build without the flag cannot be promoted.
- **The platform looks after your mail sender.** `CARLOS_MAIL` and the app's `_MAIL_FROM` setting can no longer be changed through team config.
- **`carlos ledger verify` is stricter.** It refuses a damaged ledger head with a clear error instead of crashing, and each request to the ledger host gives up after 30 seconds.
- **AWS `login_session` profiles are refused.** Commands that talk to AWS directly now stop with an error if your profile uses one, because its sign-in call can't be given a time limit. Use SSO or access keys instead.

Update your CLI to use these.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Nothing special. Roll your development deployment first, then production.
- **The console finishes its work before it stops.** On a restart it gives requests in progress up to 20 seconds to finish, then stops its background workers. WebSocket sessions close straight away. A restart can take up to 37 seconds.
- **Abandoned signed-in console requests stop waiting.** When someone closes a page or a CLI call gives up, its database queries leave the queue, so they no longer hold up other people.
- **`carlos system update` stops on an answer it can't read.** An unreadable status promotes nothing. If the console accepts a promotion but its answer can't be read, or a progress report can't be read, the command stops watching. The promotion may still be running, so follow it with `carlos system status`.
- **Streamed answers to HTTP/1 uploads are no longer cut off.** When an app started answering an upload with a declared length straight away, the edge could close its connection to the app mid-answer. Forwarded `carlos db` reads were the most likely to be hit.
- **Demo API uploads that get an early answer close their HTTP/1 connection.** If a demo API answers before an upload has finished, the edge now closes that connection after the answer instead of reusing it. HTTP/2 is unchanged. A client that sends another request on the same HTTP/1 connection opens a new one.
- **systemd queries can't hang a box's agent.** Read-only `systemctl` queries and `journalctl` now give up after 30 seconds. Starts, stops and restarts are unchanged.
- **AWS credential calls have time limits too.** Fetching credentials from STS, SSO or a container endpoint now stops if the answer stalls, as other AWS calls already did. `carlos system host-env write` without `--group` now finds credentials the same way as with it.
- **Replica placement says why it's stuck.** A stateless replica that can't be placed now logs the step that failed instead of retrying silently.
- **Region HA.** A trashed app no longer holds up a member's departure, unless it's restored or still marked for production. `carlos system group close-lost` now tells you if the member's edges record is still published. Don't delete that record by hand: termination recovery on the remaining boxes retires it. This release also refuses locks with fields from a newer storage format, so once that format is in use, don't roll back below v0.39.0.

notes.md:
#### What's new

- **See whether your config changed.** `carlos env list` now shows the bundle's version, and `--digests` adds a digest for each var. If the version or a digest is different from last time, something changed. `carlos secrets list --digests` does the same for secrets, still without showing values.
- **Write only if nothing changed.** `carlos env set`, `carlos env unset`, `carlos secrets set` and `carlos secrets unset` take `--if-version <version>`. The write happens only if the bundle is still at the version you read. If it has changed, nothing is written, `carlos` prints the current version and exits with code 4.
- **A receipt for each write.** A `set` or `unset` through a console prints what was stored: the names it set, the names it removed, any names that weren't there, and the version before and after.
- **Find out why a var isn't taking effect.** `carlos env effective --app <app> --host <host>` shows what one route gets, which layer each var comes from, and which lower layers it covers.

Update your CLI to use these. They need a v0.38.0 console. With an older console, `--if-version` is refused before anything is written, and writes print no receipt.

#### For operators

- **Roll order.** Nothing special. Roll dev first as usual, then flagship. Older CLIs work as before.
- **Console pages open during the roll still work.** Console forms now carry a token derived from the session instead of the session itself. This release still accepts the old kind, so a page opened before the roll can still be submitted. The next release stops accepting it.
- **Unit-backed apps get a syscall filter.** `carlos-app@` units now allow only the system-service syscalls, without keyring, io_uring or userfaultfd, which return ENOSYS. They also get private IPC and a read-only cgroup tree. Apps with the `doc_engine` capability keep their current filter. Unit backing is for operator-trusted tenants only: never set `--backing unit` for a tenant you wouldn't give a shell on the box.
- **Upstreams on link-local addresses are refused.** The edge, wake health checks and readiness probes no longer connect to 169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10 or fd00:ec2::254, so a route whose upstream resolves to the instance metadata service now fails. A request to port 80 whose target doesn't start with `/` now redirects to `/` on the same host.
- **Edge timeouts.** The public edge closes keep-alive connections that have been idle for 120 seconds, and gives up connecting to a remote upstream after 30 seconds.
- **AWS calls on boxes can't hang.** Every AWS client in the box's host agent now gives up after 120 seconds without response headers, or 120 seconds without receiving any data. A stalled S3 call no longer holds up a host-agent loop until the next restart.
- **Detached fleet boxes leave `carlos system status`.** After `carlos fleets detach-box`, the box no longer shows as UNREACHABLE. Its report stays in the bucket.
- **Fleet boxes start sooner.** A fleet box runs its first full pass as soon as it is ready, instead of about 17 seconds after its agent starts.
- **Runtime files.** The ten pinned runtime files in `SHA256SUMS.txt` are unchanged from v0.37.0.

bullets.md: **One command for an offline move:** `carlos move offline run --host <host> --to <region>` copies the instance's data while it still serves, then takes it offline, runs each step in turn, checks that the instance answers in the new region, and finishes the move. Before the instance opens in the new region, a failed step or more offline time than `--max-offline` allows (15 minutes by default) moves it back. After it opens, `run` never moves it back. `run --resume <move-id>` carries on a move that stopped part way. `carlos move offline status` now leads with the move's state, then shows the move, how long the instance has been offline when that applies, how long it has been in this step, whether the console is waiting on a box, and the one command forward and the one back.

**Console doors for offline moves:** Each offline move request can name its move, and the console refuses it with 409 when the host has a different move. A first `stage` can ask to create the move only, so it never restages a move someone else started. A new nudge door wakes the boxes without changing the move.

**Fleet boxes start sooner:** A fleet box no longer scans the account's HA ingress records at startup, because it never forwards HA ingress. On dev that scan held a fleet box's first reconcile back to 17 seconds after start.

**No 404 while a fleet drains:** During a fleet drain or detach, the hub can forward a host to a box before that box has set up the host's route. The box now answers 503 with `Retry-After: 2` instead of a 404 that a client might cache. Only requests the hub forwards change. A host under the platform's own domain still gets the pending page, and a request that reaches the box any other way gets the same answer as before.
**Coming from v0.35.x:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.36.0 first. Its console needs the new plan catalog, price book and price map in the same restart.
**v0.35.4 is still the rollback floor** for the console and fleet boxes.
**Update requirements:** `carlos move offline run` needs a v0.36.2 console. The startup and 503 fixes need v0.36.2 fleet boxes. Update the boxes before the console.
**Runtime files:** As in v0.34.42, this release publishes the ten pinned runtime files and lists them in the signed `SHA256SUMS.txt`. This release does not enable them.

**Leave the other dormant switches off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CARLOS_GROUP_ADMISSION`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG`, `CARLOS_BILLING` and `CARLOS_INGRESS_PROXY_SOURCES` unset. bullets.md: **Tie a fleet instance to its box:** `carlos instances label --app <app> <host>` shows which box last reported running an instance that is not tied to a box, and which box the hub sends its requests to. When the two agree, it prints the command that ties the instance to that box (`--box <box>`). Without `--box` it is a dry run and changes nothing. Only the account owner can tie an instance, and only to the box serving it now. See [carlos instances label](/docs/cli#carlos-instances-label).

**New fleet instances are tied when created:** On a fleet with more than one box, a new process instance is tied to its box when it is created. If the console cannot do that safely, it refuses the create before writing anything (`503`, code C39, `Retry-After: 30`).

**Safer fleet stops and wakes:** Before a box wakes or starts a fleet instance that is not tied to a box, it reads the instance's record again, and refuses if the record has since been tied to a box, given a copy assignment or retired. A box gives up a fleet instance only after its last saved copy is proven, and otherwise keeps it pending and retries. Moves of always-on stateless instances only go to boxes that can run them. System units are never moved.

**Log retention settings:** `CARLOS_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` (whole days, default 7) and `CARLOS_LOG_RETENTION_MB` (whole MiB per app on each box, default 50, or `off`) in a box's `host.env` set how much of each app's logs and errors the box keeps. Unset, nothing changes. A value the box can't use is logged and the default stays. The hourly cleanup also makes far fewer storage requests.

**Everything in v0.35.3:** the write fence for high availability apps, high availability when you create an app (`CONSOLE_HA_POOL_ACCOUNTS`), same-box calls, probe-burst blocking, the stateless guard and the offline move fixes. Read the v0.35.3 notes if you skipped it.
**v0.35.4 is the rollback floor.** Do not roll the console or any fleet box back below v0.35.4 once you run it. Going below it lets instances be tied to boxes without the owner. Fix problems forward.

**Update requirements:** Update every box before the console. Tying instances needs the console and every active box of the fleet on v0.35.4. A console or box that reports a build without a release number (a development build) counts as older, so the console refuses to tie instances and refuses new multi-box fleet creates.

**Apps that need a new promote:** An app on a fleet with more than one box whose current release was promoted before v0.35.4 cannot create new process instances there until you promote a release again. Retrying the create does not help.
**Coming from v0.35.2 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.35.3 first, especially `CONSOLE_HA_POOL_ACCOUNTS`.
**Runtime files:** As in v0.34.42, this release publishes the ten pinned runtime files and lists them in the signed `SHA256SUMS.txt`. This release does not enable them.

bullets.md: **Write fence for high availability apps:** On a high availability box, an instance whose replication falls more than 30 seconds behind its writes refuses new requests at once (`503`, `Retry-After: 10`), then stops and releases its host uncleanly, so another box can take over. A storage outage now loses at most about a minute of acknowledged writes, instead of up to five minutes. `carlos route --replication` now refuses `batched` and `daily` on high availability routes.

**High availability when you create an app:** An account named in the console's `CONSOLE_HA_POOL_ACCOUNTS` can create an app with high availability in a region that has a high availability pool, with the **High availability** checkbox on Create an app or `carlos apps create --region <region> --ha`. The app's first instance starts with high availability in that region's pool. The app's region and placement are then locked, and deploys swap one instance at a time. See [High availability](/docs/high-availability).

**Calls to apps on the same box:** An app can call another app on its own box by hostname again, through the box's edge on ports 80 and 443. These calls have been blocked since v0.28.17. Other ports on the box's own addresses stay closed to apps. `carlos status --layout` shows "same-box calls" as on, off (with the reason) or unknown for each box.

**Probe bursts are blocked:** A client that trips the probe-burst limit is now refused during its cool-down, with `429`, `Retry-After` and a reference code, on paths an app is not known to serve. This applies to every app. Ordinary pages, a static site's own files and fleet apps are not affected. Requests for missing site icons no longer count toward the limit. An app's record-only switch still turns blocking off, and members can now read that switch with `carlos protection`.

**Stateless builds on unassigned fleet instances:** The console refuses a stateless build for a fleet instance that is not tied to one box while the fleet has more than one active box, because no box could wake it. While such an instance runs a stateless build, the console also refuses to add a box to its fleet or bring one back.

**Offline moves:** A move's stage and start steps refuse while a box still keeps a leftover live link for the instance. A move now waits only on target boxes that can hold the instance (boxes that hibernate and serve the shared pool in the target region), and a region with no such box is refused at stage.
**Coming from v0.34.49 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.35.0 first. Everything there still applies.

**Update requirements:** The write fence, same-box calls, probe-burst blocking and the offline move fixes need boxes. High availability at create, the stateless guard and the offline move refusals need the console. Update all boxes before you update the console.

**High availability at create is off until you name accounts.** If `CONSOLE_HA_POOL_ACCOUNTS` is unset or empty, nobody can create an app with high availability, and no account can place a new instance in a pool named in any region's `ha_pools` in `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG`. Before you update the console, list the accounts that already run instances in those pools, and add their account sqids, comma-separated, to `CONSOLE_HA_POOL_ACCOUNTS` in the same change.

**Write fence:** It is on for every high availability instance as soon as its box runs v0.35.3. An instance that stops this way releases its host uncleanly. bullets.md: **Stateless replicas:** An app that keeps no local database can now run more than one copy of each instance on an owned fleet, with `carlos apps set <app> --copies N`. Each copy runs on a different fleet box. A deploy runs the release command once, then switches the copies one box at a time. When a box drains, its requests move to another copy without failing, and a request that never reached a stopped box is retried on another copy. `carlos instances list` shows one row per copy, and `carlos restart` refuses for an app with more than one copy: deploy a new build instead. Raising the count adds copies of the current build without running a release.

**Account subdomains:** A platform operator can give an account a readable name with `carlos accounts subdomain set`. Its apps then also answer at `<app>.<name>.<apps domain>`, and the console, API and CLI show that address. The address with the account's sqid keeps working. `carlos accounts subdomain remove` takes a name away; another account can take it one hour later.

**Restore checks for owners:** The backups page, the instance tile and `carlos instances backups` show the last nightly restore check of each instance. Operators get the same results for every box at `/fleet/backups` in the console and from `GET /api/cli/system/backups`. When some boxes' results cannot be read, both say so.

**Restore check fixes:** Instances whose replica holds nothing and whose database file does not exist, such as static sites, are now left out of the nightly check instead of being reported unverified every night. A fleet box without a deployment store logs one line and exits without an error. A box that cannot read its previous result publishes nothing and exits with an error.

**Schedules spread out:** An `--every` schedule now fires each instance at its own fixed point in the period, so a hundred instances on an hourly schedule wake about one every 36 seconds instead of all at the top of the hour. Add `--aligned` to keep the old behaviour. `--cron` schedules are not spread. `carlos schedule ls` shows which schedules are spread.

**Go memory limit:** A binary instance with a memory cap now gets `GOMEMLIMIT` set to 80% of its memory size, unless the app's config or `<host>.env` sets it. Seeds, `carlos run`, rootfs apps and instances under gVisor do not get it.

**Visitor country for static sites:** Every site answers `GET /.carlos/geo` with the visitor's country and the database it came from, using the same lookup as the `X-Carlos-Geo-*` headers. The answer is never cached, sets no cookie and isn't counted in analytics. The edge answers this address itself, so a file or route of your own at `/.carlos/geo` is no longer served.

**Region high availability:** A host released uncleanly after its replica was written now waits one lease term before another box takes it, so a late upload cannot overwrite the next holder's data. A clean release and a release that was never replicated hand over at once. An unclean release also hands over at once when its replica and its files were both saved and the only problem was local.

**Coming from v0.34.40 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.49 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).

**Update the boxes before the console.** More than one copy needs every fleet box, the console and every platform release channel on v0.35.0 or later, and each box's previous build too. Until then `--copies` above 1 stays off. Once the console is on v0.35.0, a box still on v0.34.x cannot retry a stateless release whose release command failed or whose result is unknown. Old boxes also read a removed account subdomain as still assigned.

**Account subdomains change who can attach hosts.** A new host directly under the apps domain now needs the creator's sqid or assigned subdomain as its label. Existing hosts keep working. After the console is on v0.35.0, and before you assign any subdomain, run `carlos accounts subdomain inventory`. It lists the labels under the apps domain that are neither an account sqid nor an assigned subdomain.

**Schedules move once.** On its first pass after the update, a box moves each existing `--every` schedule to its spread time. A box on v0.34.x cannot read a spread schedule, so update the box an instance moves to before you move it.

**PROXY protocol v2 stays off.** This release adds PROXY protocol v2 support for the region high availability load balancers. It stays off until you set `CARLOS_INGRESS_PROXY_SOURCES` and follow "PROXY protocol v2 on the region NLBs" in the region high availability runbook. Once a box has that setting, it refuses to activate any build without PROXY protocol v2 support, which means any build older than v0.35.0. That includes a rollback to the previous build.

**Update requirements:** Stateless replicas need the console, the boxes and every platform release channel on v0.35.0 or later. Account subdomains need boxes, then the console. bullets.md: **Nightly restore checks:** Every box now restores the saved copy of each of its instances every night, checks it, and publishes the result. The check starts at 03:00 UTC plus a random delay of up to 30 minutes, restores the oldest copies first, and has 45 minutes to finish. Each box writes its own record in the deployment bucket, `control/verify/<box reference>.json`, and updates it every 10 minutes, so you can read the results without signing in to the box. A copy is marked failed only when the check proves it is damaged. A copy the check could not read, for example because of a storage fault, is marked unverified. A box in a group checks the instances its group assigns to it, and its own instances that are not in the group. Boxes in the home region run the check too. The check reads the saved copies without changing them. It skips an instance while an offline move of it is waiting to be finished. If the instance's record, or the stored version of it, changes during the check, the result is unverified.

**Alerts for restore checks:** Three new operator alerts report the results: `verify_failed` for an instance whose check proves damage, `verify_unverified` for an instance that stays unverified three runs in a row, and `verify_coverage`, one per box, when an instance on it has had no passed or failed result for more than seven days since it was first seen.

**Forms on demo apps:** Demo apps now send `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` instead of `no-referrer`. With `no-referrer`, Chromium sent `Origin: null` with a form submitted on the same site, so the demo app's form protection refused it. Other sites still get no referrer.

**Claim page for demo apps:** The page for claiming a demo app now shows one line per account, with its plan, usage and room left. Sponsored accounts no longer show an unlimited value or an empty usage meter. Accounts that cannot take the app are listed last, and a search box appears when there are more than six accounts. After you return from signing in, the progress view appears first. Its bar never moves backwards, and it says when the claim is taking longer than expected or is still finishing. The last page links to the app in the console, for current members, and to its live address.

**Coming from v0.34.40 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.48 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).

bullets.md: **Backups:** `carlos instances backups --app <app> --instance <host>` shows, for one instance, when its last change was saved, how far back its history reaches, and the status of its database and files. It shows no contents. Any member of the account can run it, as can deploy, operate and admin credentials. A console on this release also shows the same facts in a Backups section on the instance page.

**Instance logs:** On a box that runs instances under the pinned runtime files, an app that wrote a log while starting could stop before it served any requests. Its output did not reach the app logs or the box logs. Output from these apps now reaches both. Boxes that use systemd, the default, were not affected.
**Moves:** Copying a database during an instance move no longer starts background compaction. A late compaction could change the copy during the move and make the move fail.

bullets.md: **Linked deployments:** A self-hosted deployment on one box can now link to an account on a CARLOS console, such as Carloku, and publish its apps there at public addresses. Apps with instances can be published. Static sites and apps with a password cannot yet. The apps keep running at home, and the console carries their traffic through its tunnel. Run `carlos link create --to <console URL>` on the home box, then approve the link in a browser within ten minutes. `carlos link` and `carlos links` publish, unpublish and unlink, and the account's Fleet tab lists linked deployments. While home is offline, visitors see an offline page. See the linked deployments page in the docs.

**Statistics retention:** A console can now delete visitor statistics older than a set number of days. Set `CARLOS_ANALYTICS_RETENTION_DAYS` on the console to a whole number of days, for example 400. Statistics from the last 400 UTC days are kept, and older ones are deleted. Left unset, nothing is deleted, as before. The console runs at most one pass a day. `CARLOS_ANALYTICS_RETENTION_DRY_RUN=1` logs what a pass would delete without deleting it. An invalid value stops the console from starting.

**Group rolls:** `carlos system group` now tries a read up to four times when AWS throttles it or a request gets no response, instead of refusing at once. Writes and failed sign-ins are never retried. A release whose new launch template differs from the old one only in its user data no longer needs the group pinned back before the next roll. Any other difference still needs the pin-back. Bare `carlos system group`, `-h` and unknown verbs now print the group help.
**Demo apps:** If demo serving was turned off while a demo request was being handed to a box, the console closed that box's demo connection. It now skips the request and keeps the connection open.

**Coming from v0.34.40 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.45 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).
**Update requirements:** Linked deployments need the console, the CLI and the home box. Statistics retention and the demo fix need the console. The group roll changes need the CLI.

**Statistics retention and old versions:** The deployment bucket keeps old versions of each file. To delete the old versions of expired statistics too, set `enable_analytics_version_prune` in the `region-host` infrastructure module, which gives the console box the permissions it needs. Without them, the console deletes only the current files and logs the missing permission.
**Runtime files:** As in v0.34.42, this release publishes the ten pinned runtime files and lists them in the signed `SHA256SUMS.txt`. This release does not enable them.

bullets.md: **Size check for fleet apps:** For an app placed on a fleet, the console now checks the requested size against that fleet's active boxes only. Before, it also counted the platform's own boxes, so a small platform box that the app can never run on could cap its size. If the account does not own a fleet the app is placed on, the console cannot read that fleet, so it refuses sizes above standard.

**Load balancer drain for fixed boxes:** A fixed box that is a target of a network load balancer can now leave the load balancer before its edge stops. The box fails its own health check, waits until the load balancer's target groups have stopped sending it traffic, waits 10 more seconds, closes its public listeners, and only then stops its apps and its edge. This happens on `carlos system apply`, on a rollback, on a manual restart of the edge, and on a reboot. It is off unless `CARLOS_INGRESS_TARGET_GROUPS` is set in the box's `host.env`. Boxes in a group are not affected. While a box drains, a request that would wake an app gets a 503 with `Retry-After`.

**Coming from v0.34.40 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.44 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).
**Update requirements:** The size check change needs the console. The load balancer drain needs boxes.

**New unit on every box:** The update installs `carlos-edge-drain.service` and orders every app unit to stop after it. With `CARLOS_INGRESS_TARGET_GROUPS` unset, its stop returns at once and stops behave as before. The update service's start timeout goes from 15 minutes to 20 minutes.

**Turning on the drain:** Set `CARLOS_INGRESS_TARGET_GROUPS` only after the box can read its target groups' health (see `docs/region-ha-runbook.md` and the `region-host` infrastructure module). The update that first brings a box onto this release is not drained, because the binary already on the box runs that update and does not drain.
**Runtime files:** As in v0.34.42, this release publishes the ten pinned runtime files and lists them in the signed `SHA256SUMS.txt`. This release does not enable them.

**Leave the other dormant switches off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CARLOS_GROUP_ADMISSION`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG`, and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset. bullets.md: **Long host names start again:** A host name longer than 40 bytes gets a shortened instance ID that starts with "_". Since v0.34.34, the check that confirms a newly started instance refused that ID, so the box stopped the instance straight away, without logging a reason, and visitors got a 503. The check now accepts these IDs.

**Every 503 says when to retry:** Every 503 that a box's edge or activation path writes now carries a `Retry-After` header. The one exception is the page for a site whose plan no longer covers it, because waiting changes nothing there. These 503s also carry `X-Carlos-Answer`, a short name for the reason, and `X-Carlos-Box`, a tag for the box that does not reveal its label. A 503 from the app itself is passed on unchanged.

**Health checks and HTTPS redirects (from v0.34.42):** An app that redirects plain HTTP to HTTPS, such as a Rails app with `force_ssl`, now passes its health check. The check no longer follows redirects, and it sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, as the edge does for real requests. Before, such an app never became healthy and kept restarting. This applies to wakes on boxes and to `carlos ship --check`.
**Clearer failure reasons (from v0.34.42):** A failed health check is no longer reported as a staging failure just because the app's host name contains the word "staging".

**Replication settings apply on update (from v0.34.42):** When an update changes the replication service unit file, the box now restarts the service if it is running, so the new settings take effect. In v0.34.40, the old process kept running with the old settings. The config file written by `carlos ops litestream` now sets logging to warnings and errors only. It reaches a box the next time that command runs there.

**Coming from v0.34.40 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.41 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).
**Long host names:** The fix is in the boxes. An affected app does not need to be shipped again.

**Replication restart:** A box coming from v0.34.39 or older restarts a running replication service once during the update. A box already on v0.34.40, v0.34.41 or v0.34.42 has the new unit file, so the update does not restart it. The config file setting reaches a box the next time `carlos ops litestream` runs there.
**Runtime files:** As in v0.34.42, this release publishes the ten pinned runtime files and lists them in the signed `SHA256SUMS.txt`. This release does not enable them.

**Update requirements:** The long host name fix, the 503 headers, and the health check and failure reason changes apply to boxes. The same health check change in `carlos ship --check` needs the CLI. The replication change needs boxes. This release has no console changes.

**Leave the other dormant switches off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CARLOS_GROUP_ADMISSION`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG`, and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset. bullets.md: **Pages cached at the edge:** An app can send `Carlos-Page-Cache: on` with a page, and a `Cache-Control` such as `public, s-maxage=31536000, max-age=0`. The box that runs the app keeps a copy and serves it without waking the app. The copy lasts until it expires, until the app clears it with `Carlos-Purge` or the control socket, or until the instance gets a new release or new config. A new `Carlos-Purge` value, `all`, clears every host of the instance, including its aliases and custom domains. Copies are kept and served only for visitors who send no cookies and no `Authorization` header. The "Caching pages at the edge" section of the CLI guide has the details.
**`carlos instances set-pages`:** turns page caching off or on for one instance. `off` discards its cached pages and returns the instance to the five-minute response cache.
**Getting started links to secrets:** The secrets step on the console's Getting started card now links to Settings > Environments for your first live app.
**App pages on a console with no bucket:** App pages on a console with no bucket configured now render. Actions that need the bucket are refused with a message.

**Page caching is off until you turn it on.** Set `CARLOS_PAGE_CACHE=1` in a box's `host.env` to let apps on that box use it. The box also needs the asset cache (`CARLOS_ASSET_CACHE=1`). The setting is read when the agent starts. In this release only the box that runs the app keeps pages. Instances that run as `carlos-app@` systemd units, and instances in a region HA group, are not cached yet.

**What needs which update.** Page caching needs the boxes. `carlos instances set-pages` needs the console and the CLI. The Getting started link and the no-bucket fix need the console. Boxes and consoles can be updated in either order.

bullets.md: **Edit settings and secrets in the console:** Account members can now add, change and remove settings on the app's Settings page, under Environments. All environments comes first, and a named environment uses its value for anything it does not set itself. One Save changes one environment. Secrets are sealed in your browser with the app's key before they are sent, so you can replace a secret but never read it back. Setting a secret on the page needs JavaScript; `carlos secrets set` still works from a terminal. Saving does not restart anything. After you save, the page says for each copy of the app when it should pick up the new values.

**Clearer notices after `carlos env set` and `carlos secrets set`:** Against a v0.34.32 console, the CLI now tells you for each host whether it will get the new values and restart by itself, pick them up when it next wakes or starts, needs you to check a background worker, or could not be checked. Against an older console, it prints the same notice as before.

**A clearer answer during an edge restart:** A request that reaches a box while its edge is shutting down now gets a 503 with `Retry-After: 10`. It gets the same "unavailable" answer as a closed admission, instead of "instance failed to wake".
**Managed fleets groundwork:** More console work for managed fleets is in place. It remains off and has no production effect.

**Coming from v0.34.30 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.31 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).

**What needs which roll.** The settings page needs the console. The new CLI notices need both the console and the CLI. The edge restart answer needs the boxes. Boxes and consoles can roll in either order. Until a box runs v0.34.32, the console cannot tell whether that box restarts background workers by itself, so it asks you to check those workers.

**Leave the other dormant switches off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CARLOS_GROUP_ADMISSION`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG`, and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset. Do not set `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any `host.env` file or run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are. Existing zero-downtime deploy and database-read forwarding settings continue to work.

bullets.md: **Alerts on unusual demo activity:** The console can email its system operators and ops owners when demo use looks unusual. It sends one when demo create attempts come close to the daily limit, when many creates come from a few addresses or from one network block (an IPv4 /24 or an IPv6 /48), when refused creates spike, or when abuse reports arrive. It sends one email for each condition while that condition remains true. A daily digest lists new abuse reports when any arrived. Emails contain aggregate counts only. They never contain IP hashes, report details, demo names or claim tokens. To enable alerts, set `CONSOLE_DEMO_ALERT_ENABLED=true` on the console and restart it. The console sends through its verified mail sender or the operator's existing Keymail grant, to the addresses in `CARLOS_SYSTEM_OPERATORS` and to the ops owners. Other `CONSOLE_DEMO_ALERT_*` settings change the thresholds. An invalid setting prevents the console from starting.

**Coming from v0.34.28 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.30 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).

**What needs which roll.** This release changes only the console. Boxes need nothing new, and the CLI is the same as v0.34.30 apart from its version. Even when alerts are off, the console stores a salted prefix hash for each admission and refusal counters for each minute. It keeps this data for 24 hours.

bullets.md: **Bring back a deleted instance:** Deleting an instance keeps its database. Run `carlos instances create --app A --host H --restore` to bring it back on the same host with that data. A service credential with the `instance` role can send `"restore": true` to the create door. Restore works only for a plain instance that the same app in the same account deleted. The instance must have been created after restore became available and deleted after that. Restore it from the console in the region where it lived. Instances with a seed, import, pool, fleet placement or high availability are not eligible. Anything else is refused with the reason, and nothing is written.

**System call filter for tenant instances:** Tenant instance units now use systemd's `@system-service` system call set, minus io_uring, the kernel keyring and userfaultfd. A blocked call returns `ENOSYS`, which means “function not implemented”. Runtimes that can fall back continue to work. Go, Node, Python, Ruby and PHP apps were checked and serve normally. The isolation probes check the filter from inside the instance and log the result.

**Instances stop cleanly:** Stopping an instance now sends its main process one SIGTERM, waits up to 18 seconds for it to exit, and only then sends SIGKILL. Before, systemd could sometimes send SIGKILL straight after SIGTERM, so the app had no time to finish its work.
**Demo claim page:** The demo claim page shows live progress while your demo is copied and started. A refused claim link now moves focus to the page heading, so screen readers announce the reason.

**Coming from v0.34.27 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.28 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).

**What needs which roll.** Restore needs a console roll and this CLI. The system call filter and the clean stop need a box roll, and each instance picks them up when it next starts. High availability group members keep their pinned version until you re-pin them.

**Leave the other dormant switches off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CARLOS_GROUP_ADMISSION`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG`, and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset. Do not set `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any `host.env` file or run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are. Existing zero-downtime deploy and database-read forwarding settings continue to work.

bullets.md: **Getting started card:** A Getting started card now appears at the top of the account apps page. It lists four steps: connect your agent or terminal, put your first app live, add your app's secrets, and use your own domain. The first two steps tick themselves when they are complete. You can mark the other two done or skip them. Each person can hide the card and show it again. The card stays hidden once every step is complete.

**CNAME advice for custom subdomains:** On a deployment with `CONSOLE_REGION_INGRESS` set, non-apex custom domains now get CNAME advice. Point a CNAME for the subdomain at the deployment's steering hostname. You can also point an A record at the fixed ingress addresses. Apex domains still get A record advice because they cannot use a CNAME. Deployments without steering are unchanged. The domains API adds a `cname_target` field to its domain rows.

**Departed group members are cleaned up when nobody serves their pool:** When no surviving box in a region serves a departed high availability group member's pool, the departure used to stay open. The member's edges file and status snapshot remained. A box now records the host as unserved when the member's lock is a release marker or past expiry. It does not import the app or write a lock. The departure finishes within three minutes after EC2 shows that the member is gone.

**Coming from v0.34.26 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.27 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).

bullets.md: **Log an agent in by tapping a link:** `carlos auth login` now prints a link to open and a short code. Open the link in a browser already signed in to the console. The page shows the code, so check that it matches what your agent or terminal shows, then press **Approve**. You no longer type the code. After you approve, the page tells you to go back to your agent, which carries on by itself.

**Agents that only show output at the end:** Some agents, Claude Code among them, only show you a command's output when the command ends. For those, run `carlos auth login --no-wait`. It prints the link and the code, then exits. Once the person has approved, run `carlos auth login --wait` to finish. A code lasts ten minutes.

**A clearer approval page:** The page title is now "Approve a sign-in". It shows the code in large type, the label supplied by the machine, the remote address and, where known, its country and subdivision code. It says when the sign-in started. If you did not ask for it, press **That wasn't me**.

**Old static sites are cleaned up while the box runs:** Boxes used to remove old copies of static sites only when the edge started, so a site with many large versions could fill the disk. The edge now cleans up after each handler switch, following a 30-second settling period, and every hour. It keeps the current and previous versions, along with versions used by live handlers or in-flight requests. The box disk alert also fires earlier, while there is still room for the disk floor plus two of the largest kept static trees.

**Terminated group members hand over at once:** When a high availability group member was terminated, its apps could answer `503` for about 15 minutes, until its lease expired. During a planned termination, the edge now stops in the right order and releases the member's high availability leases while it shuts down. Another member can then take over straight away.

**Coming from v0.34.25 or older:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.26 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first, and boxes go before the console (see v0.34.6).

**The agent login needs the console and the CLI.** Roll the console and update `carlos` for the agent login. The static site cleanup and the group member hand-over need a box roll. High availability group members keep their pinned version until you re-pin them.

notes.md:
**`carlos accounts migrate` and a floor that names a commit**

When the hostname history floor names only a commit, a build from that exact commit can pass. Other builds cannot tell whether they include it, so `carlos accounts migrate` refuses migration. The old message said this carlos was older than the floor and told operators to update. It now says the floor names a commit, not a release, and points to `console hosts-used raise-floor`.

**For operators**

- **The hostname history's floor:** `console hosts-used activate` now refuses a console that isn't a release build, so a new floor always names a release and its commit. If `carlos system hosts-used status` shows a floor with no release, such as `floor: 50c0cb14 (50c0cb14…)`, roll this release to every console and box, then run `console hosts-used raise-floor -release v0.34.4 -checkout <platform checkout>` with the v0.34.4 console. It names the console's own release as the floor, after checking that its commit contains the floor's. Builds older than v0.34.4 are refused by the floor from then on. See "The history's floor" in the platform README.

- **Anonymous demo apps:** demos get edge protections: a warning banner, a strict Content Security Policy, host-only cookies, lifetime request and byte caps, an operator serving switch and takedown (`carlos system demos`), and an abuse report queue. Protections stay off until `CARLOS_DEMO_EDGE_PROTECTIONS=1` is set on the console and every demo ingress and serving box. While unset, the console refuses demo creates and updates, and edges refuse demo traffic. So demos remain closed even when `CARLOS_DEMO_APPS=1`. Follow "Anonymous demo apps in development" in the platform README to open them. A deployment with demos off is unchanged.

- **Region HA group mode:** group boxes now stage the bootstrap outside `/run`, where Debian 13 blocks programs from running, and use the same install permissions as fixed boxes. Group mode stays off by default, and fixed boxes are unchanged.

- **Coming from v0.33.x:** read the "For operators" notes of v0.34.0 to v0.34.3 before you roll. A console with `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS` set needs a valid `CONSOLE_HA_CAPACITY_CONFIG` first.

- **Every other dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CARLOS_GROUP_ADMISSION`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset, don't put `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any host.env, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are: a box armed for zero-downtime deploys stays armed, and a console that forwards database reads keeps forwarding.


The console is published for self-hosting as `carlos-console-linux-amd64` and `carlos-console-linux-arm64`. Verify it against `CONSOLE_SHA256SUMS.txt`, whose signature `CONSOLE_SHA256SUMS.txt.sig` uses the same key.

**Markdown versions of static pages**

A static site can now ship a Markdown file beside an HTML page: `page.md` beside `page.html`, or `index.md` beside `index.html`. The page keeps one URL. A request whose `Accept` header prefers `text/markdown` over `text/html` gets the Markdown, and every other request gets the HTML, with `Vary: Accept` on both. **Failed stateless releases are held (preview, dev)**

When a stateless app's release command fails, or its result is unknown, the release is now held, as it already is for apps with a database. Wakes keep using the last build whose release passed. - **Account creation:** owners of the deployment's ops account are no longer refused by the free-account cap when they create an account, through `carlos accounts create` or the console.
