notes.md:
**Stateless apps (preview, dev)**

`carlos ship --stateless` ships a release that keeps no local database: it gets no SQLite file, no `CARLOS_DB`, no restore and no Litestream. A stateless release starts only on boxes running v0.34.0 or later. The console refuses it while any box on the app's channel is older. One copy per app for now. This is a preview on the dev deployment.

**Litestream memory cap**

`carlos ops litestream` now sizes the replicator's memory cap from the number of databases it replicates: 256 MB plus 8 MB a database, and never less than 512 MB. It writes the cap to `carlos-litestream.service.d/50-memory.conf`. The unit's own default rises from 256 MB to 512 MB, and its restarts back off to one a minute. A platform service on a box that restarts more than three times in ten minutes now raises a restart-loop alert.

**Domains**

The domain purchase page in the console is now one card with a four-step list that follows the purchase until the domain is live.

**For operators**

- **Region HA:** when a box is terminated, a surviving box takes over its timers and due wakes without waiting for visitor traffic. This stays off unless region HA is on.

- **Every other dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset, don't put `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any host.env, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are: a box armed for zero-downtime deploys stays armed, and a console that forwards database reads keeps forwarding.

bullets.md: **Each instance's secrets now have a sealed copy in the region's storage.** The box keeps a sealed copy of each instance's `<host>.env`. It also keeps sealed copies of the `instance.key` and `report.token` files an app keeps at the top of its own directory. These copies are stored in the region's data bucket. Each copy is sealed to the box's secrets key and bound to your app. Only a box that can already read your app's secrets can open it. When a box starts an instance whose `<host>.env` is missing, it puts the sealed copy back first. This keeps the instance's `CARLOS_ADMIN_TOKEN` and `CARLOS_INSTANCE_KEY` instead of giving it new ones. A file that is there is never replaced. You can edit other values in `<host>.env`. The box seals the new contents within a minute. `CARLOS_ADMIN_TOKEN`, `CARLOS_INSTANCE_KEY`, `instance.key` and `report.token` cannot change once sealed. If the box finds a different value, it refuses to start the instance and raises an alert. Deleting the file does not reset it. A box without the secrets key a copy was sealed to will not start that instance. This includes a box whose key was changed. Put the old key back.
**On boxes, rootfs app processes now get HOME=/tmp when nothing else sets it.**
**A box needs its `CARLOS_SECRETS_KEY` for instances that have a sealed copy.** A box whose key changes refuses those instances until the old key goes back.
**Roll an HA region's boxes together.** Update them back to back, with no other box in between.
**A box rolled back to an older release can publish a raw env again.** The box that reads the manifest raises an incident alert and names the affected host and the box that saw it.
**A fleet's secrets key can't be replaced while the fleet has instances.** This includes instances in the trash.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console, and roll a dev deployment before production.** Coming from v0.33.0 or earlier, read the [v0.33.1 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.33.1) first, and the notes they point to. bullets.md: **A fleet box could refuse to start an instance whose local copy it had to set aside (v0.33.0 and v0.33.1).** When an instance's local database on a fleet box is not marked for the box's current assignment, the box moves that copy aside and restores the instance from the fleet bucket. On a nested-layout box, that move failed, so every wake for that instance was refused and it answered 503. Now the copy is set aside, nothing is deleted, and the instance starts from the bucket on its next wake after the box updates.

**`carlos devbox serve` runs on macOS.** launchd binds the port and hands the open socket to the service, which runs as its own user, and `--env-file` reads its settings from a private file. infra/devbox/README.md has the steps.

bullets.md: **A terminal on your instance: `carlos run -it` and `carlos console`.** With -it, the command runs in a terminal session instead: what you type goes to it and its screen comes back, so a REPL or a shell works. `carlos run -it --app shop --instance shop.example.com -- bin/rails console` opens one. `carlos console --app shop --instance shop.example.com` opens the console process your app's manifest declares, in a terminal session, as carlos run -it would. carlos ship fills one in for Rails, Laravel and Django apps when the manifest has none. An app without one is refused, and the message says how to name a command instead.

**Sessions are off until an owner turns them on.** `carlos apps set shop --interactive on` lets any member open a terminal session on the app's instances with carlos run -it or carlos console. A session can read and change everything the instance can, so it is off until an owner turns it on. Any member can turn it off.

**Sessions have limits, and they are audited.** A session ends when the command exits, after 30 minutes without a keystroke, after 6 hours, or soon after your connection drops. A deploy, a restart or a move of the instance ends it too. Ctrl-C and Ctrl-D go to the command. One session at a time per instance, beside any run. Who opened it, where, when it ended and how are in the audit log. What you type and what it prints are not kept. A session exits with the command's own status, 124 when it ended for lack of keystrokes or at 6 hours, 125 when it was interrupted or its box's connection dropped, 130 when you cancelled it before it started, 3 when the box refused it or none opened it within 60 seconds, 2 when the console refused it, and 1 when carlos lost its connection to the console.

**`carlos run` works on rootfs apps and on customer fleets.** For a rootfs app the command after -- runs inside the instance's image and is found on the image's PATH. On a customer fleet, the instance's box reaches the console for the run itself, so carlos run works there as it does on any other box.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console, and roll a dev deployment before production.** Coming from v0.32.2 or earlier, read the [v0.33.0 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.33.0) first, and the notes they point to. Sessions need both the instance's box and the console on v0.33.1.

**The binary probe gains a pts-private line.** It checks that an instance cannot reach one of the box's terminals. `/dev/pts` lists nothing and `/dev/ptmx` cannot be opened. While the new binary runs under the old probe unit during the roll, the line reads unverified. After the roll, check that every box is still ready for nested instances.

**Sessions need the release signing key and the nested layout.** The console must hold the release signing key, and the instance's box must be on the nested layout. A console with host claims armed refuses every session.

**Plans can sponsor the accounts that existed before plans went on.** Set `sponsor_accounts_before` in the catalog to a time no later than the console's start, like `"2026-11-01T09:00:00Z"`, and every account created before then that has no plan of its own is sponsored with no limits before any limit applies to it. If the console can't do that when it starts, it runs with plans off and logs why. A sponsored account can ship daemon and always-on releases on shared boxes.

bullets.md: **Operators get fleet alerts in Slack, by email or by signed webhook.** The console now runs an alert engine. Once a minute it reads every box's alerts and, every five minutes, its heartbeat, groups what is firing into incidents and sends them to the connectors set up on /fleet/alerts: a Slack incoming webhook, an email address, or an https webhook signed with Ed25519. Each connector is confirmed before it receives anything else. A box now warns when its disk is on course to fill within 72 hours, so there is time to act before it fills. Other rules cover a box that stops reporting, a platform service that is down, a certificate that expires within 14 days, and disk, memory and CPU use as before. Each message says what is wrong, how much time there is and what to do, and links to the incident and to a snooze for 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week. One rule firing on several boxes is one message. The engine can send later updates and daily reminders while a condition continues. In this release alerts go to the deployment's operators only. App owners can't subscribe to them yet.

**`carlos deploy` creates a missing app and its first instance.** `carlos deploy --app shop --env PORT=8080 ./shop` creates the app and its first instance if they don't exist yet, then deploys the binary and waits for it to serve. Existing instances stay as they are. `--region` picks a new app's region, and checks an existing app's region. `--env KEY=value`, repeated, sets ordinary variables before shipping, on a new app or an existing one. Values are not printed but stay in your shell history, so use `carlos secrets set` for secrets. An app in the Trash is not restored.

**On a fleet with two or more boxes, each instance runs on one box.** The console chooses the box, and traffic goes straight to it. If a box stops reporting for 20 minutes, its instances move to the others. `carlos fleets drain <fleet> <box>` moves a box's instances off it. A box that has run instances detaches only with `carlos fleets detach-box --terminated`, once its machine is gone, so drain it before you terminate the machine. `carlos fleets ls` gains a LABELS PAUSED column. Fleets with one box work as before.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console, and roll the console straight after its boxes.** Coming from v0.32.1 or earlier, read the [v0.32.2 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.32.2) first, and the notes they point to. From the box roll on, a box's own webhook and SNS topic carry only `disk` and `engine_silent`. Until the console rolls, the other warnings reach operators only by the old watcher's email.

**The alert engine replaces the alert watcher.** On its first pass the console takes over what the watcher already mailed, so a rule already firing is not announced again, and gives each operator an already-confirmed email connector for their sign-in address. A console with host claims does not start the engine. After the roll, check that /fleet/alerts lists each operator's email connector as On, and that the "Alert checks" job on the operator dashboard ran in the last minute with no note. Beside console.db, `alert-connectors.key` (32 bytes, mode 0600) should exist and `alert-engine.beat` should change every minute. Back up `alert-connectors.key` off the box. It is kept out of the database replica on purpose, and without it every Slack and webhook connector needs its URL again after a restore.

**A box's own sinks now carry only the two alerts that matter when the console is down.** `CARLOS_ALERT_WEBHOOK` and `CARLOS_ALERT_SNS_TOPIC_ARN` get `disk` (the disk is full now) and `engine_silent`. Memory, CPU, mail relay lag, location database and the disk forecast reach operators through the alert engine. A Slack incoming-webhook URL in `CARLOS_ALERT_WEBHOOK` now gets a body Slack accepts. To have the console box page its own sinks when the engine stops, set `CARLOS_ALERT_ENGINE_BEAT=/data/console/alert-engine.beat` in that box's host.env once the console has rolled and the file exists, then restart its agent. The README's "Fleet alerts" section has the details.

**Placing instances on boxes stays off until every box runs v0.33.0.** The console places a fleet's instances only when the fleet has two or more active boxes and every box in the deployment, platform and fleet boxes alike, and the console itself run v0.33.0 or later. A fleet with a sidecar, or with an instance the platform does not run, keeps today's behaviour, and a sidecar can't be created on a fleet with more than one box. If a box in a placed fleet later reports an older release, the console stops moving that fleet's instances, logs an ERROR naming the fleet, box and version, and `carlos fleets ls` shows `yes` under LABELS PAUSED until the box is updated.

**The ops account is exempt from plans.** The deployment's built-in ops account has no plan limits, caps or billing, and owning it doesn't count as anyone's free account. `carlos accounts plan` on it says so and changes nothing. If it was under a plan before, the console removes its limits record and cap rows.

**The operator activity pages group bursts.** The /fleet dashboard's Latest activity shows one row per person: when they were last active, how many actions, the latest one and on which apps. /fleet/activity folds a run of actions by one person on one account and one app, each within 10 minutes of the last, into one row you can expand. A CLI ship followed within 10 minutes by the promote of the same build by the same person on the same account and app shows as one row. Stored audit rows are unchanged.
**With billing on, Checkout takes a VAT number.** A business customer can add one at checkout, and Stripe Tax applies reverse charge for qualifying EU business sales.

**Every other dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset, don't put `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any host.env, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are: a box armed for zero-downtime deploys stays armed, and a console that forwards database reads keeps forwarding.

**`carlos devbox` gives your dev server an HTTPS link on a shared development machine.** On a machine that an operator has set up on the tailnet, `carlos devbox share --port 5173 shop` publishes a link such as https://shop.devbox.example.com to your own dev server, and live reload passes through. `carlos devbox share --dir ./dist docs` publishes a folder instead, with its `_headers` rules. changes.subject: Fix the #471 tunnelclient flake in TestRoundTripUpgradeEndsWithItsContext/during_the_handshake (test only, no production defect). The test cancelled once the hub had the box's marked 200, but that does not mean the box's Hijack had returned: x/net (v0.60.0, serverConn.writeHeaders) queues the reply to the flush before the 200 reaches the wire, and the handler then selects on that reply and on the stream's close. When the handler goroutine had not run by the time the hub's RST_STREAM was processed, both were ready and Go picked at random; picking the close made Hijack fail with "http2: stream closed", the fixture returned before its conn Read, and the test's wait for that Read timed out. The hub did reset the stream on every run; the box only learned of it in Hijack rather than in Read, which is correct behaviour (the box edge's reverse proxy treats a failed hijack as an error and closes the app conn). The fixture now closes boxEnd.hijacked once Hijack returns, and the test waits for that event as well as the hub's handshake hook before cancelling. Before: 88 of 200 runs failed without -race on DOCS-T1. After: 200/200 under -race, 200/200 without, 500 per -cpu=1,2,4,8, package -count=20 and go vet clean.

bullets.md: **Apps on a fleet can use WebSockets at their public URL.** A WebSocket to an app placed on a fleet, such as a Rails app's Action Cable connection, now reaches the app through the platform's router. The router carries it down the fleet's tunnel to the box that runs the app. The app's own handshake reaches the browser unchanged, so subprotocols and compression work. The router applies the app's rate limit and plan throttle when it admits the WebSocket, and closes open WebSockets when the account is throttled.

**Open WebSockets close when the app stops being served there.** If the router stops serving the app for the account, app or fleet that opened a WebSocket, for example because the app moved, its route was removed or the box left the fleet, the socket closes within seconds.
**The rails-shop sample has a live page.** Its counts update over an Action Cable socket, and the page reconnects with capped backoff after the socket drops.

There is no release floor and no switch: nothing refuses an older box, and nothing needs turning on. Once the hub is updated, a 502 from a box that is not yet updated shows in the app's availability errors as "the fleet box runs a release that cannot carry WebSockets".

**Each fleet box carries at most 128 open WebSockets.** The next one gets a 503 with `Retry-After: 5` and the page "Too many open connections to this app's box. Try again shortly." The app's availability errors list it as "the fleet box has too many open connections". A slot frees as soon as a socket closes.

**A tunnel route with its password page on the box now takes the password through the router.** The router passes the login down the tunnel to the box only when the login is for that tunnel route itself.

bullets.md: **An app on a fleet now has a public URL.** Place an app on a fleet and it answers at its public URL through the platform's router, with its certificate and any custom domain attached to it. Nobody writes a route by hand. The router passes each request down the fleet's tunnel to the box that runs the app. The app's rate limit and plan throttle apply once, at the router, and the fleet box still shows the app's password page.

**If another route already holds the name, it keeps it.** An existing route is not overwritten. A hand-written route keeps serving, and requests do not reach the fleet. The deployment's operator can remove the route.

**Route commands leave a fleet app's host alone.** `carlos add`, `carlos route` and `carlos remove` refuse a forward host for a fleet app, because its route follows the app's instance record. Change the app instead, with `carlos apps place` or `carlos instances delete`.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.31.1 or earlier, read the [v0.31.2 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.31.2) first, and the notes they point to.

**The hub serves fleet apps.** The hub is the box that holds the fleets' tunnels: the console's box, with `CARLOS_TUNNEL_HOST` set and `CARLOS_FLEET` unset. It writes a forward route for each instance placed on a fleet that the instance's account owns. It updates or retires that route when the instance moves or is deleted, and retires it when the app is put in the trash, unless production retention keeps it. Nothing runs on the hub for these apps, and the hub never answers one from its caches. A fleet box can now bind only hosts of its own fleet. Before this release, a fleet box could steer another fleet's host.

**Check your fleet routes before rolling.** A route that already holds a host keeps it, and the hub writes no forward route there. A route placed on a fleet whose account does not own that fleet is no longer served by the hub. Before rolling, check that every route on the hub that sends requests to a fleet belongs to the account that owns that fleet.

**v0.32.0 is a release floor while any fleet exists.** An older hub serves forward routes but cannot remove them. So while a fleet exists, the console refuses to move a channel below v0.32.0, or to publish a channel's first release below it. `--allow-below-fleet-forward-floor` on `carlos system update` and `carlos system rollback` overrides that. A hub below the floor keeps serving fleet apps it can no longer remove, so remove their routes first. Creating a fleet is refused until every channel is on v0.32.0 or later, unless that channel was published with `--allow-below-fleet-forward-floor`.
**WebSockets do not cross the fleet tunnel yet.** An app on a fleet answers ordinary requests at its public URL, but a WebSocket connection to it through the router does not reach the box.

**Every other dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset, don't put `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any host.env, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are: a box armed for zero-downtime deploys stays armed, and a console that forwards database reads keeps forwarding.

A forward for a born-HA host that cannot connect to its holder now marks that holder suspect for 10 s (holderSuspectTTL) in the activator's holder cache instead of dropping the entry. While a host is suspect, ForwardTarget answers a refusal (edge.ForwardDecision{Refuse: true}, which replaces the bare ref string) and the edge's frontForwardHA answers it at the front door with the existing unreachable answer, 503, Retry-After: 10, "instance is waking elsewhere; retry shortly", with no lock read, no dial, no note, no local wake and no per-request step (N-HA10 kept). After the window the next request reads lock.json once; if it still names the same box, only the caller that read forwards (one dial), queued callers are refused, and the box is suspect again until that forward's outcome says otherwise. bullets.md: **Response headers for a static site.** Put a `_headers` file at the top of a static site to set response headers on the paths you choose, in the format Netlify and Cloudflare Pages use: a path on its own line, then its headers on indented lines below it. You can set `Cache-Control`, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` and `Timing-Allow-Origin`. Paths match the way `_redirects` sources do, against the address the browser asked for, and every matching rule applies, with the lower rule winning for the same header. The headers are sent with files served normally, including 304 and range responses, but not with redirects, not-found pages or errors. A `Cache-Control` rule replaces the default `no-cache`. `carlos ship` and `carlos deploy` refuse a `_headers` file with a line they cannot use, or any other header, and name the line. A file can have up to 100 paths. A site without a `_headers` file is served exactly as before.

**`carlos logs` names the process of a rootfs app.** Each line from a rootfs app carries `process=web`, `release` or the worker's declared name, so `carlos logs --field process=web` shows only the web process. In `carlos instances list`, `HEALTH` for an instance placed on a fleet comes from its fleet box: `Running`, `Asleep`, `Failed`, or `unknown` when the box's view is not available yet.

**Clearer exits for rootfs processes.** A rootfs process that was killed is now reported as a failure, not as `instance exited (exit 0)`. A worker that ended without any exit status says it is starting again, and `REASON` for a held build says why that build failed on the box.

**`carlos ship --check` keeps its data between containers.** The check's data volume now survives from the release container to the web container, so migrations run in the release step are still there when the app starts.

The console's purchase screens change, but billing stays off while `CARLOS_BILLING` is unset.

bullets.md: **One address for each folder on a static site.** When a folder with an `index.html` is requested without its trailing slash, such as `/blog/post`, it answers with a 301 whose `Location` is the relative `./post/`. The query string is kept. This gives the page one address for analytics and makes relative links resolve against its folder. The automatic redirect does not apply to files. A folder without `index.html` remains a 404. The site's `_redirects` rules are checked first. A rule naming the path, or a rule that would redirect its slash form, prevents this automatic redirect so the request is handled as asked.

**One custom domain, one instance per region.** A regional domain is served in each named region by that region's own instance of the app. A request is answered in the region it reaches and is never sent to another region. If that region's instance is not running, the request gets a 503. Create one with `carlos domains placements --app shop --set ie=shop-ie.example.net --set uk=shop-uk.example.net example.com`, and add `--wildcard --catchall` when creating its one-label catch-all. Without `--set`, the command shows each region's instance, whether it is ready, and the addresses to use for latency-based DNS. A hostname already attached as an ordinary domain, or covered by a catch-all, is refused. An existing regional claim can have its placements replaced, but `--wildcard` and `--catchall` cannot be changed after creation. Path prefixes, static sites, fleet placements and TCP-backed targets are not supported on a regional domain. The domains list, domain details and settings page show it as `regional`.

**Each fleet gets its own secrets key.** If you run your own fleet, secrets and credentials the console creates for apps placed on it are sealed to that fleet's key. The private half stays on the fleet's boxes. The platform receives only the public half. An app on a fleet cannot hold a secret until its fleet has a key. Set one up in this order:
1. Update your `carlos` CLI to v0.31.0 or later. The console refuses a secret from an older CLI for a fleet app.
2. Run `carlos secrets genkey` to make the pair.
3. Put the private half in `/etc/carlos/host.env` on every box as `CARLOS_SECRETS_KEY`, then run `systemctl restart carlos-edge` on each box.
4. Register the public half with `carlos fleets secrets-key <fleet> <pubkey>`, or use `carlos fleets secrets-key --file <path> <fleet>` with a file containing `CARLOS_SECRETS_PUBKEY=` or the bare key. Only an account owner can register it. The command prints the fingerprint.
5. On each box, run `carlos secrets fingerprint`. Its fingerprint should start with the first 12 characters after `sha256:` in the `SECRETS KEY` column of `carlos fleets ls`.
6. If registration lists values that the fleet's boxes cannot open, set each one again with `carlos secrets set --app <app> <var>=<value>`. For a credential the console created, run `carlos store rotate --app <app>` or `carlos email rotate --app <app>`. The `STALE` column of `carlos fleets ls` counts what remains.

**Boxes and console both change.** The static-site redirect, regional-domain serving and named-unit config delivery change the boxes. Regional-domain placement, fleet-key registration and sealing, and named-unit route records change the console. The fleet secrets key itself has no box-side change in this release. Roll the boxes first, then the console, as always. Coming from v0.30.2 or earlier, read the [v0.30.3 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.30.3) first, and the notes they point to.

**Config delivery to named units needs a declaration.** A route stamped with a systemd unit (`carlos route --unit`) can now get its config from the box's root pass. Root renders the config to `/etc/carlos/apps/<host>.env`, writes a drop-in under `/etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/` that makes the box's `/etc/carlos/units/<unit>.base.env` and that file the unit's only environment files, reloads systemd and restarts the unit. It does this only for a unit that `/etc/carlos/named-units.json` names with the route's host, account and app. Nothing happens without that file, so a box with none behaves as on v0.30.3. Each stamped unit needs a line in the file before delivery starts. Install the file with `carlos system named-units install <file>`, as root, and do not edit it by hand while carlos runs. Removing a unit's line is what removes its drop-in. A unit that loads any other environment file, or a variable named in both the base file and the route's config, is refused and the reason is logged on the box.

**v0.31.0 becomes a floor once a regional domain exists.** Creating a regional domain is refused until every box, and every channel a box follows, is on v0.31.0 or later. From then on, no channel moves below v0.31.0 unless you pass `--allow-below-regional-floor`, because a box below it cannot read regional domains and stops serving them. Until someone creates a regional domain, nothing changes.

Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are: a box armed for zero-downtime deploys stays armed, and a console that forwards database reads keeps forwarding.

bullets.md: **A clearer Analytics tab.** Page views, visitors and data served lead the tab. Sizes use KB, MB and GB, and counts are grouped, like 1,284. Hover over, focus or tap a column on the chart to see its numbers, and move between columns with the arrow keys. Hours that have not happened yet are left empty, and the period still in progress is marked. Under the chart are the busiest hour or day and, for 7 and 30 days, the average per full day. Pages, referrers, countries and events are listed with their share of the total. Known countries show their names and flags. If an edge restarted during the period, one note says counts may be missing for the affected day or days.

**Traffic on the Overview.** An app's Overview page now shows its page views and visitors for the last 7 days, with the same chart and a link to the Analytics tab. The page waits up to 300 ms from the start of the request for the numbers. If they are still loading, it says so. If the read fails, it says that traffic could not be read and links to Analytics. If analytics is off and there are no saved numbers, the card explains how to turn it on. If saved numbers remain from when it was on, the card shows them and says analytics is off.

**Analytics pages load faster.** Settled days are cached for up to six hours, and files in a range are read concurrently. Once a 30-day view has warmed the cache, a later view reads today's and yesterday's files, two per box, not thirty, plus the box listing.

**A thank-you after you buy a plan.** After a completed purchase, owners see a thank-you panel on the billing page only when the account has a live paid subscription. It names the account and its new plan. When the plan limits are available, it says how much room the plan gives. It always links to Go to your apps. Add packs appears when packs can be added. Upgrade appears when a higher plan is available. The plan summary lists each pack on its own line, like "4 Apps packs", and currency codes are shown in capitals, like USD.
**Typing a pack quantity replaces the 0.** On the billing page, a quantity box selects its number when you click or tab into it, so the first digit you type replaces it.

**Console only.** Every change in this release is in the console. The boxes get the new build but behave as on v0.30.2. Roll the boxes first, then the console, as always. Coming from v0.30.1 or earlier, read the [v0.30.2 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.30.2) first, and the notes they point to.

**The Overview reads analytics.** Each app's Overview page now reads that app's last 7 days of analytics, beside its other reads. The page waits at most 300 ms from the start of the request for them, and the counts are kept for a minute, so reloading the page does not read them again.

bullets.md: **Rootfs apps can run workers.** A rootfs app can declare up to four worker processes beside its web. Each worker uses the same image and environment as web. Workers start after web is healthy. If a worker exits, the platform restarts it with a delay that doubles from two seconds until it reaches a one-minute cap. A worker that keeps crashing never takes web down. Rootfs apps run only on boxes your account owns: a fleet owned by your account, or any box in a deployment that serves one customer.

**Rootfs apps are documented.** A new Rootfs apps page in the docs says what an image is started with, what it can write and where it can run. A Rails guide takes a Rails 8 app from a Dockerfile to a running instance, with web, a job worker, a release process for migrations, and uploads to the app's own bucket. Notes for Laravel and Django say what differs for those frameworks. The finished app is in the platform repository under `examples/rails-shop`. `carlos run` does not reach rootfs instances yet.

**Check a rootfs release with placeholder settings.** `carlos ship --check --env KEY=VALUE` gives every process in the check a variable, such as a placeholder secret. Repeat it for more than one. The check never reads the app's real config or secrets. It sets `CARLOS_SOCKET`, `CARLOS_DB`, `CARLOS_HOST` and `CARLOS_REGION` itself, so `--env` cannot set those, and `--env` without `--check` is refused.

**See a rootfs instance's runtime and workers.** `carlos instances list` has two new columns. RUNTIME says `rootfs`, or `rootfs, hibernates` for an instance that sleeps when idle. WORKERS counts the instance's running workers out of the ones it declares. If a worker reaches the restart limit after repeated crashes, WORKERS names it as restarting. A binary instance shows `binary` and `-`. `carlos instances create` says whether a new rootfs instance is always on or hibernates, and `carlos apps place` refuses a rootfs app.

**Billing changes reach Stripe again.** On a console with billing on, every change the console sent to Stripe failed with no response, such as starting a payment, opening the billing portal or changing a quantity. They now go through.

**A clearer billing page.** The billing page shows a summary of your plan, a card for each plan with what it includes, a currency switch and a row for each pack. Native form controls across the console follow its dark theme. Continue to payment shows a spinner for at least 650 ms and cannot be pressed twice. Without JavaScript, the form submits as before.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.30.1 or earlier, read the [v0.30.1 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.30.1) first, and the notes they point to.

**A freshly bootstrapped box can use its agent before its first reboot (#446).** `carlos bootstrap` now applies the box's temporary-file settings before it starts any unit. Before, the control socket directory could be owned only by root, so the agent could not use it until the box rebooted. With region HA, an instance created on a new box also gets the nested layout paths it needs immediately, before the box has chosen its default layout.

**Workers change nothing until a release declares one.** A box runs no worker until a rootfs release declares workers. Each box now reports its instances' worker states, which `carlos instances list` shows in WORKERS.

**Every other dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset, don't put `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any host.env, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are: a box armed for zero-downtime deploys stays armed, and a console that forwards database reads keeps forwarding.

bullets.md: **Team credentials.** A new service role, `team`, is for a server that provisions instances for teams inside one app without reaching the app's own config. Mint one with `carlos services create --role team --app <app> --scope <scope> <credential-name>`. It reaches only the environments its scope owns, the instances bound to them and their hostnames. It never sees the app's default config, and anything outside its scope answers as if it did not exist. An account owner marks an environment with `carlos env adopt --app <app> --environment <environment> --scope <scope>`, clears it with `carlos env release --app <app> --environment <environment>`, and copies it with `carlos env fork --app <app> --from <environment> --to <new-environment> --scope <scope>`. An owned environment never inherits the app's default config. When email is provisioned, it gets its own SES sending user and key. When relay is enabled, it gets its own relay identity. Binding an instance into one takes `--scope <scope>` on `carlos instances create` or `carlos instances set-environment`.

**A rootfs app's deploy overlaps.** A rootfs app's deploy now overlaps: the new web starts beside the serving one, after its release process, instead of the instance stopping for the deploy. Releases that ask for hold still hold.

**Rootfs apps can run a release process.** A rootfs app can declare a `release` process, such as a database migration. The box runs it from the new image before the new web serves, and the new web serves only after it passes. A failed or timed-out release marks that build failed. A cancelled release, a release the box cannot prove stopped, or a lost lease aborts the attempt without marking the build failed. During an overlap deploy, the old web keeps serving in all of these cases. Workers and `carlos run` for rootfs apps come in a later release, and rootfs apps are not documented yet.

**Fewer 502s while a box's own services restart.** When a local service on the box itself restarts, such as the console, the edge holds requests while it retries for up to 13 seconds instead of failing them immediately with 502 or 503. A route with health checks can wait longer for readmission, up to 30 seconds total.

**Faster CLI writes.** `carlos ship`, `carlos instances create` and `carlos apps create` now do independent reads at once. Instance and app creation also read less. `carlos promote` reads the release manifest and pipeline at once. A release manifest larger than 1 MiB now fails the ship check. On a test copy shaped like a large deployment, measured after the request body was read, instance create went from about 2 seconds to about 0.6 seconds, ship from about 1 second to about 0.4 seconds, and app create from about 1 second to about 0.4 seconds. No write happens in a different order.

**A new hostname's first certificate waits for every edge.** On a deployment with more than one edge, the first certificate order for a new hostname waits up to 45 seconds after the issuer first sees the name. This gives the other edges time to learn the name before certificate validation starts. A one-edge deployment does not wait.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.30 or earlier, read the [v0.29.0 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.29.0) first, and the notes they point to.

**Owned environments need every box on v0.30.0.** The console refuses to create an instance in an owned environment, or to move one into it, while any fresh box in the placement where the instance could run, or its current host when it is fresh, is on a release older than v0.30.0. It names that box. An older box would add the app's default config to the owned environment.

**Owned environments get their own AWS users.** Installing this release by itself creates nothing in AWS. An owned environment of an app with email provisioned gets its own SES sending user and key. It gets its own relay identity when the app's relay is enabled. These credentials are created as ownership and the relevant service converge, and are removed when the environment is released.

**The edge's own restart is unchanged.** The 13-second wait covers services on the box, not the edge itself, so a box roll still has its short gap. Each edge start now logs one `edge: listeners:` line naming the ports it bound.
**An agent restart fails a rootfs deploy.** If the box agent restarts while a rootfs deploy is under way, that deploy fails. Retrying it runs the release process again for the new attempt.
**The hourly adopt pass removes the old join units.** A box that left the join-era build by a hand roll no longer keeps `carlos-system-join.path` and `carlos-system-join.service`.

**The console is faster and its scan pass stops failing.** Several slow operator pages now read the bucket in parallel. `/fleet/economics` also keeps settled usage days between views. The scan pass now skips old app release prefixes that appear before account names, instead of failing on them every run.

**The console has a speed budget.** Warm pages, which make no S3 or box request before their first byte, have a 150 ms budget. Cold pages, which make at least one such request, have a 500 ms budget. A change is timed from when the console has read the whole request body to its first byte and has a 500 ms budget. The Console speed section on `/fleet/metrics` shows pages and changes separately. The background jobs table shows each job's total and average S3 requests. The CI performance check uses median timings for its gate, so these budgets are targets rather than a promise that every request finishes within them.

**Every other dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset, don't put `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any host.env, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are: a box armed for zero-downtime deploys stays armed, and a console that forwards database reads keeps forwarding.

changes.subject: Platform rolls: the edge holds requests to a restarting local upstream instead of answering 502/503 (#434 option 2). A loopback TCP or unix-socket upstream that refuses, or whose socket is missing, is redialled every 100 ms for up to 13 s under one deadline set when the dial starts (unix upstreams already had this window and now share the code); non-local upstreams are unchanged. A probed route with a local upstream waits for the prober to readmit it, never dialling an ejected upstream: 13 s plus the prober's real readmission time, capped at 30 s (19 s with default health settings). The edge binds :80/:443 before serving and logs one 'edge: listeners:' line naming them. No socket unit, and no unit, root, updater or rollback change: the socket (option 3) comes later in a release that refuses rollback below the first socket-aware build (Paul's ruling, #434). Local witness TestLocalUpstreamRestartWitness: 0 failed requests across tcp, unix and probed routes during an upstream restart under load; 2126 x 502 with the hold off. bullets.md: **Boxes can run a rootfs app's web process.** A rootfs app is an OCI image shipped with `carlos ship --rootfs`. Its always-on instances now start on a box that has passed its rootfs check, take new releases with an overlap swap, stay awake, and restart after a crash. They run only on boxes your account owns: one of your fleets, or any box of a single-tenant deployment. Workers, the release process and `carlos run` for rootfs apps come in a later release, and rootfs apps are not documented yet.

**Creating a rootfs instance checks where it can run.** The console refuses a rootfs instance outside your account's own boxes, in a dedicated pool, seeded from another database, or as a replica. It also refuses one while any box it could run on is on a release older than v0.29.0, and names that box. An app's first rootfs release is refused while the app still has instances made for a binary app. Moving a rootfs app's instances, or placing the app somewhere else with `carlos apps place`, is refused.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.29 or earlier, read the [v0.28.30 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.30) first, and the notes they point to.

**v0.29.0 is a rollback floor.** Once a channel points at v0.29.0 or later, `carlos system update` and `carlos system rollback` refuse to move it to an earlier release, because an earlier box cannot run rootfs instances. A hand-run `carlos system apply` on a box running v0.29.0 or later refuses an earlier release too. Pass `--allow-below-rootfs-floor` to do it anyway. A box's automatic rollback after a failed update is not affected.

**The box agent changes.** It runs rootfs instances through their whole lifecycle. The first boot of a rootfs instance writes a marker beside its replica, `<hibernate prefix>/rootfs-initialized/<incarnation>.json`, and a box that finds the marker but no database or replica refuses to start the instance empty. When it adds a socket-backed instance record with no runtime and no existing row, the agent reads the app's kind marker once per app per pass. Binary instances, static sites and services behave as before.

**Leave `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_SINGLE_TENANT` unset on a shared deployment.** It is a new console setting for a deployment that serves one customer, and it lets that customer's rootfs instances run on any ready box in the deployment, not only on a fleet box that account owns.

**The hostname history scan copes with busy boxes.** `scripts/hosts-used-scan-aws.sh` now lists each box into a snapshot file in `/run` and pages that, so a box whose files change while it is listed can be scanned.

**Every other dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS`, `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST`, `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` and `CARLOS_BILLING` unset, don't put `CARLOS_BOX_REFERENCE=group` in any host.env, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. Keep `CARLOS_SWAP` and `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD` as they are: a box armed for zero-downtime deploys stays armed, and a console that forwards database reads keeps forwarding.

bullets.md: **The first part of high availability in a region. It stays off until you turn it on.** A new console setting, `CONSOLE_HA_REGIONS`, lists the regions whose new instances are born highly available. Such an instance can wake on any box in its region, and only one box serves it at a time. This release turns it on nowhere. Instances that exist today keep working exactly as before, and are never converted.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.23 or earlier, read the [v0.28.24 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.24) first, and the notes they point to.

**The box agent changes.** Each lease lock now names the box, its instance id when known, and the process id. For instances that exist today, the lock is still deleted when the instance sleeps. For an instance born highly available, the box writes a release marker instead of deleting the lock. Another box takes the instance only after a clean marker. A box reuses its own local copy only when the marker names that box, the lifetime matches, and the local state is unchanged. Otherwise it restores the instance from storage. bullets.md: **Edges can keep copies of an app's asset folders.** On an armed box, the edge can keep copies of cacheable files under the folders an app declares with `carlos deploy --assets` or `carlos ship --assets`, and answer later matching requests from those copies. An armed box in another region can fill its copy from the app's home box, so a visitor far from home can get the file from a nearer box. For cache-eligible requests, `Carlos-Cache` is `miss` when the box fetched the file for a cache fill, even if the copy was not ultimately stored, `hit` when it answered from its copy, and `bypass` when it forwarded the request without using the cache. Nothing is copied until an operator arms a box.

**The asset cache stays off until you arm a box.** To arm one, set `CARLOS_ASSET_CACHE=1` in its host.env and restart it. The copies live in `asset-cache` under the box's data directory. Only an armed home box publishes an app's assets to other boxes. In dev, arm the home box for a test app first. Then arm one box in another region and verify that it can fetch the app's asset from the home box before arming the rest. On the flagship, arm the console box first, then one small box and watch its disk, then the rest one at a time.

bullets.md: **`carlos deploy` and `carlos canary` can check a host behind a password gate.** Deploy asks the console for a pass that lasts 15 minutes and checks the new version through the gate with it. The console only hands one to someone who could already remove the gate, or to a deploy credential for a host on a channel it can deploy its own build to, and each one is recorded in the app's activity log.

**The edge records requests for well-known attack paths.** It checks each request against a list built into the platform, such as `.env` and `.git` files, path traversal and common probe paths. By default it blocks nothing: a match is recorded and the request goes on to the app. `carlos explain <code> --app <a>` says which rule fired and when, and shows the request if it is still kept, for up to 7 days.
**An offline move's pause is a few seconds shorter.** At the first wake after a move opens, the new box removes the staged copy's files 8 at a time instead of one by one.
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.15 or earlier, read the [v0.28.16 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.16) first.

**Nested instances can no longer connect to their own box's addresses.** Each box denies its interface addresses, its private IPv4 and any global IPv6, on `carlos-instances.slice`, so every nested instance is refused a connection to them. The box's isolation probe now also checks that deny (`box-addr`) and that a nested instance using the default memory setting cannot map memory that is both writable and executable (`mdwe`). If the probe fails, the box stops waking nested instances. After the roll, read `/run/carlos-control/probe.out` on each box, dev boxes first.

**Boxes can run rootfs apps, but none run yet.** A box can run an app shipped as a read-only image as a nested instance, on an account's own boxes only (a fleet with an owner record, or a single-tenant deployment), with `CARLOS_SWAP=overlap`. Each box reports `rootfs_ready` in its status. Nothing changes until a rootfs release is shipped.
**Leave `CARLOS_EDGE_PROTECT` unset.** Unset, every rule only records. `block` answers a 404 block page and is for dev boxes only. `off` turns the checks off.

**Instance lifetimes wait for `carlos system lifetimes cutover`.** Until an operator runs it, the console works as before. Run it only after every box runs this release and the old console has stopped. It is done once per deployment and cannot be undone, and after it no older console or box may run in the deployment again. Leave `CARLOS_LIFETIMES_MIGRATE` unset. While a console starts, until it has read `control/lifetimes-cutover.json`, every page answers 503 for a moment.

**Plan caps add a slowdown and a lapse, and still do nothing without a plan catalog.** With `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` set, an account past twice the month's bandwidth, or past twice its awake hours after 3 days' notice, has its instances share 5 requests a second, with bursts up to 30, until the month ends. When a paid plan or pack falls, what the smaller plan no longer covers is turned off after 7 days of grace: visitors get a plain 503 page, it is never woken, and its settings and data are kept. Owners choose what stays on the account's keep page, and paying again turns everything back on. Without a catalog, nothing changes.

**Regional display names stay off until `STATUS_NAME_REGION` is set.** Set to a region code such as `ie`, it gives the box a display name such as `seamus-minding-ie` on the status page and in the console. Nothing is keyed on it and the box's label is unchanged.

**Asset copies can be declared, but nothing copies them yet.** `carlos ship --assets` and `carlos deploy --assets` declare folders for an app's build files. `carlos instances set-assets` turns copying on or off for one instance, and `carlos assets` inspects or purges copies. bullets.md: **An instance can have rate limits.** `carlos ratelimit show` displays four numbers per instance, while `set` and `clear` change them for one instance or every instance of an app: when it counts as busy, how many requests one address may have in flight while it is busy, and a backstop rate and burst per address. A path prefix such as `/api/` can have its own share, rate and burst. A refused visitor gets `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After`, and a refused request never wakes a sleeping instance. In the default observe mode, a box only counts what it would refuse until the deployment's operator turns enforcement on. The docs' "Rate limits" page says more.

**A new custom domain gets checked for a certificate sooner.** Once a host is attached, the certificate issuer checks its DNS every minute for ten minutes, then every five minutes for the rest of the hour. If DNS points at the deployment, it can order the certificate before the next hourly pass, subject to the shared certificate order limit.

**The edge keeps request records in an app's logs.** It records a sample of requests that found nothing. It keeps path pieces and query parameter names only when they are short or look like harmless lower-case words, and masks the rest. It also records a count of the app's requests each minute. `carlos logs --stream edge` shows them.

**Static sites: old cache versions are cleaned up at startup when the edge is alone.** On the first start that creates the cache lock, the edge only creates the lock. A later start can set aside old release trees and remove them in the background when no other edge is serving the cache.
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.14 or earlier, read the [v0.28.15 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.15) first.

**Rate limits only count until you set `CARLOS_RATE_LIMIT=enforce`.** Each box reads it from its `host.env`. Unset or `observe`, a box counts and logs what it would refuse and refuses nothing. `off` turns the limiter off. Read the counts with `carlos ratelimit show` for a few days, then set `enforce`, dev boxes first.

**Disk use under `/data/static` can drop after the second edge start on this release.** At startup, an edge that is the only one using its static cache sets aside old release trees and removes them in the background, while keeping each site's current version. The first start on this release only creates the cache's lock file, so cleanup starts from the next start.

**Plan caps still do nothing without a plan catalog.** With `CARLOS_PLAN_CATALOG` set, a console now refuses new always-on workers and schedules that run more often than the plan allows on shared boxes, while allowing them on an account's own boxes. It warns owners at 80% of each cap, keeps a grace clock for each cap, pauses account-wide email senders immediately when the account reaches twice the plan's daily limit, unless the catalog sets a lower ceiling, and refuses new uploads after storage grace and three days' notice, or immediately at twice the storage cap. Without a catalog, nothing changes.

**The `deployment-buckets` and `region-remote-host` modules expire old data versions.** In their data buckets, a replaced or deleted version is kept for 7 days (`data_noncurrent_days`) before it expires. Unfinished uploads are aborted after 7 days, and empty delete markers are cleaned up. Until then, a deleted file can still be brought back.

bullets.md: **Instances wake from sleep faster.** A box now makes fewer requests to the deployment's storage while it wakes an instance.

**A service can run an app's commands.** An account owner can mint a `run` credential with `carlos services create --role run --app <app> --commands "<prefixes>" <name>`. It can start, follow, cancel, expire and acknowledge runs of that app's instances, only for commands that start with one of the prefixes it was minted with, and it sees only the runs it started. A prefix also allows every flag and argument after it, so grant the shortest one that names the work. `carlos run --idempotency-key <key>` starts a run at most once while the key remains recorded, on a console that has turned keys on. The console keeps a key for 24 hours or until that caller makes 32 newer keyed admissions on the same instance. The CLI reference's "Runs from a service" section says how.
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.12 or earlier, read the [v0.28.13 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.13) first.

**A console that sends email needs a permissions boundary before it rolls.** On this release, a console with `CARLOS_MAIL_REGION` set must have `CARLOS_MAIL_USER_BOUNDARY` set to the ARN of a customer managed policy in the same account. Create that policy so it allows `ses:SendRawEmail` and nothing else. Set the variable on every such console and grant the console role `iam:PutUserPermissionsBoundary` and `iam:ListUsers` before you roll. Existing sending users receive the boundary when a relevant mail operation reaches them. To cover users that no operation reaches, set `CARLOS_MAIL_BOUNDARY_SWEEP=1` on one console and restart it. If the sweep reports users that are not bounded, fix the cause and run it again. A console without `CARLOS_MAIL_REGION` needs nothing.

**Leave `CARLOS_RUN_KEYS` unset until every box runs this release.** Without it, a run request with an idempotency key is refused with 503 `keys_not_ready`. After every box runs this release, set `CARLOS_RUN_KEYS=on` so the console accepts keyed run requests. This is a one-way switch. A box rolled back to an older build forgets the keys, and a retry could then start a second run.

bullets.md: **A static site can ship a `_redirects` file.** Put it at the top of the site directory, in the format Netlify and Cloudflare Pages use: one rule per line, with a source, a destination and an optional status. A rule can redirect, serve another file at the same URL for a single-page app, or serve the not-found page. A file at the requested path wins unless the status ends in `!`. `carlos ship` and `carlos deploy` refuse a line they cannot use, and name it. A site without the file is served as before.

**`carlos db query` can read an instance whose data is in another region.** Where the deployment has turned this on, the query runs in that region and only the rows come back, encrypted for your terminal on the way. There, the copy can be at most 2 GB once restored, the query runs for at most 5 minutes, and the rows can total at most 64 MB. An older `carlos` is asked to update. `carlos db pull` cannot fetch a copy from another region yet.
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.** Coming from v0.28.8 or earlier, read the [v0.28.9 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.9) first.

**Forwarded `carlos db query` is off until the console sets `CARLOS_DB_FORWARD=1`.** Before you set it, apply the deployment bucket's `db-reads/` lifecycle rule from this release's `deployment-buckets` module. Forwarded reads delete nothing, so without the rule nothing under `db-reads/` is ever removed. The console sends a read only to a region where a box publishes `db-read-1` in its edges file. Boxes set up for database reads in v0.28.9 publish it, and list the read queue every 30 seconds. A console with host claims on does not forward. To turn it off, unset the variable and restart the console.

**An offline move can copy most of its data before the instance goes offline.** Run `carlos move offline stage --host <host> --to <region>` while the instance keeps serving. It refuses unless that build is what the box holds, then installs the new console and keeps the old one as `console.prev`. No hand recovery is needed. **A nested instance's `config.env` is written as soon as its directory appears.** Before, a move could leave the instance without it for up to an hour.

**Each offline move step now sees a current box report.** While a move is running, the source boxes and the sealing box report again every 15 seconds. A move takes under a minute of downtime when its steps run back to back. A step that meets a stale report now says the report is not current and to try again. Before, `flip` could answer that a process was still running.
**A source box's scheduler leaves a moved instance alone.** After `open`, it no longer writes a stray token file into the instance it gave up.

**Roll the boxes first, then the console.**
**Coming from v0.28.3, read the [v0.28.4 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.28.4) first.** They all still apply.

**`carlos move offline` moves one instance to another region, with planned downtime.** It is for operators, works only while host claims and Phase 1 moves are off, and takes one step per command: `start`, `seal`, `flip`, `open`, then `finish`. The instance is offline from `start` until `open`. Until `open`, `abort` puts it back where it was with nothing lost.

**Roll every box in both regions before you start an offline move.** `seal` waits until every box in the instance's current region has stopped it and said so, and a box on an earlier release never says so.

**A box whose guard is armed on v0.28.4 needs one update by hand.** Its updater reads a candidate's progress messages as part of the answer, so `carlos system update` refuses every candidate on that box. Stop `carlos-system-update.path`, put the v0.28.5 binary in a root-only file after checking it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, run it as root as `system apply` with the box's `host.env`, check the box, then start `carlos-system-update.path` again. Do one box at a time. From then on the box updates as usual.
**The guarded updater reads only what a candidate writes to standard output.** Progress and warnings no longer break its checks, so this is the last update a guard-armed box needs by hand.
**`carlos system guard-arm` makes its directories readable whatever your umask is.** Before, a root shell with a strict umask left them unreadable to the box's updater.

**Routes with their own unit now restart on boxes whose agent doesn't run as root.** The agent now hands those restarts to root. Before, the restart was refused, the agent read that as a broken build and rolled back.
**`carlos system status` warns when a new box would boot an older build.** It compares `bootstrap/carlos` with stable's build and says which file to copy over it.

bullets.md: **`carlos run` runs one of your app's commands against one instance.** `carlos run --app shop --instance www.example.com -- <command>` runs it as that instance, with its environment and database, and prints the output as it arrives. `--file` uploads files with the run, up to 64 MB in total. `--timeout` sets how long it may take, 30 minutes by default and up to 6 hours. `--follow <id>` reattaches to a run already started. It needs an instance on the nested layout.

**New instances can start from a copy of another instance's database.** `carlos instances create --from <host>` copies the source's replica, so the source keeps serving. `carlos instances import` brings an instance the platform never ran onto it, from a snapshot of its database. Both refuse until your operator turns them on.
**The download is smaller again.** The linux/arm64 binary is about 46 MB, down from about 78 MB.
**Nothing else changes for people using the CLI.**
**Roll the boxes first, then every console.** A run is refused until the console that records it is on this release.

**Coming from v0.26.x, read the [v0.27.0](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.27.0) to [v0.27.3](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.27.3) operator notes first.** They all still apply.
**Instance control restarts with this update.** `carlos system update` does that on its own. A box updated any other way needs `systemctl restart carlos-instance-control` afterwards.
**Give the console room for run uploads.** The console holds a run's uploaded files, up to 64 MB per run, in its temporary directory until the box takes them.

**Seeded instances stay off until you publish the seeds floor.** `carlos instances create --from` and `carlos instances import` refuse until `carlos system seeds-floor publish` names a release every box runs. Publishing it is one way: from then on no box recovers to an older build. Leave it unpublished until you have decided to turn seeding on.

**The host claim is still off.** This release carries the claim's protected host state and the `carlos system claims` activation commands, but nothing uses them while `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM` is unset. Errors from a route that has no app are now filed so the claim's checks can read the bucket.

**Every dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_SWAP`, `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_APP_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS` and `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST` unset, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`.

bullets.md: **Restarting the edge no longer leaves an instance unreachable for 15 minutes.** If the edge stopped while an instance was waking, the instance could stay locked until its lease expired, and every request to it was refused for up to 15 minutes. The stopping edge now cancels the wake, makes sure it has stopped, and lets the lease go. If it cannot confirm the stop, it keeps the lease, as before.

**New accounts never get a reserved address.** An account's address is part of every app's hostname. Account creation now skips any address that spells a name the platform uses itself, such as dev, edge or www. Existing accounts keep theirs.
**Nothing else changes for people using the CLI.**
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.**

**Roll the console as well as the boxes.** Only a console on this release skips reserved account addresses when it creates an account.

**Every dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_SWAP`, `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_APP_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS` and `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST` unset, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. bullets.md: **Root keeps its own record of each box's releases.** A box's root process now keeps the builds it has seen run healthy, and the build each service ran before its current one, in directories only root can write. Before, it read them from places the platform's own service could write. Restarts, rollbacks and recovering from a bad build work exactly as they did.
**Nothing changes for people using the CLI.**
**Roll the boxes first, then the console.**

**Coming from v0.25.x, read the [v0.26.0 operator notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.26.0) and the [v0.26.1 notes](https://github.com/carlosframework/releases/releases/tag/v0.26.1) first.** They all still apply.

**Before rolling, check two things on each box.** `/`, `/var` and `/var/lib` must be owned by root and not writable by group or others, and `/var/lib/carlos-claims` must not exist. If either check fails, root can't update a service that has its own unit, such as the console, on that box, and logs `repoint failed: permission denied` on every pass.

**Health history starts empty.** Root no longer reads the health history the service kept before this release. Don't add a `require` or `prove` entry for a service to `/etc/carlos/proof-policy.json` until both its current build and the one before it have been seen healthy since the roll. Otherwise rolling back to the earlier build waits for a proof.

**One earlier build per service is kept.** `/opt/carlos/previous/<host>` points at the build each service ran before its current one, and the box keeps that build when it prunes old versions. Disk use can grow by up to one build per service.

**`carlos __cgexec` can appear in `ps`.** Each new instance process now starts through a short-lived helper that places it in its cgroup before it runs. For a few milliseconds `ps` can show `carlos __cgexec` as a child of the agent. Monitoring, or a `pkill` that matches "carlos" in a command line, can catch it.

**After the roll, check placement on each box.** `journalctl -u carlos-edge --since '<roll time>' | grep 'placement before exec failed'` should print nothing. A line there means a process was moved into its cgroup after it started instead. That affects resource accounting, not serving.

**Every dormant switch stays off.** Leave `CARLOS_SWAP`, `CARLOS_MOVES_PHASE1`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_ORIGINS`, `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM_RETIRED_LOCATIONS`, `CARLOS_CONSOLE_ID`, `CARLOS_REGION_HA`, `CONSOLE_APP_REGIONS`, `CARLOS_TEMPORARY_APPS` and `CARLOS_REQUIRE_POINTER_DIGEST` unset, and don't run `carlos channels digests on`. With `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM` set, instance control now refuses to start until a later release.
